the items of businesses mentioned below.

NOTES:
1. An Explanatory Statement pursuant to Section 102 of the 
Companies Act, 2013 (“the Act”) in respect of item nos. 
3 to 7 of the Notice set out above, is annexed hereto. 
The Board of Directors has considered and decided to 
include item nos. 3 to 7 as Special Business as they are 
unavoidable in nature. The relevant details as required 
under Regulation 36(3) of the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (Listing Obligation and Disclosure 
Requirement) Regulations, 2015, (“Listing Regulations”) 
and Secretarial Standard on General Meetings (“SS-2”), 
issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India, 
of persons seeking appointment / re-appointment as 
directors are also annexed.
2. In accordance with the provisions of the Act, read with 
the Rules made thereunder and Circulars issued by the 
Ministry of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”) and the Securities 
and Exchange Board of India (“SEBI”) (“the Circulars”), 
companies are allowed to hold Annual General Meeting 
(“AGM”) through video conference/other audio visual 
means (“VC/OAVM”) till further orders by MCA, without 
the physical presence of the Members at a common 
venue. Hence, in compliance with the Circulars, the AGM 
of the Company is being held through VC/OAVM. 
3. The attendance of the Members attending the AGM 
through VC/OAVM will be counted for the purpose of 
reckoning the quorum under Section 103 of the Act.
4. The proceedings of the AGM shall be deemed to be 
conducted at the Registered Office of the Company i.e. 
‘B’ Wing, Ahura Centre, 2nd Floor, Mahakali Caves Road, 
Andheri (East), Mumbai 400 093 which shall be the 
deemed venue of the AGM. Since the AGM is being held 
through VC/OAVM, the route map for the venue of the 
AGM is not required to be provided.
5. KFin Technologies Limited (“KFin”), the Company’s 
Registrar and Transfer Agent (“RTA”) will provide the 
facility for voting through remote e-voting [hereinafter 
called as “e-Voting Service Provider (ESP) ”], for 
participating at the AGM through VC/OAVM and for 
e-voting during the AGM.
6. Generally, a member entitled to attend and vote at a 
meeting is entitled to appoint a proxy to attend and vote 
on a poll instead of himself and the proxy need not be a 
member of the Company. Since the AGM is being held 
through VC/OAVM, physical attendance of Members 
is dispensed with and consequently, the facility for 
appointment of proxies is not applicable. Hence, proxy 
forms and attendance slips are not annexed to this 
Notice. 7. The Register of Directors and Key Managerial Personnel 
and their shareholding, maintained under Section 170 
of the Act, the Register of Contracts or Arrangements 
in which the Directors are interested, maintained under 
Section 189 of the Act, certificate from the Company’s 
Secretarial Auditors certifying that the Company’s ESOS 
Schemes are being implemented in accordance with the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India (Share Based 
Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021, 
will be available for inspection by the Members through 
electronic mode during the AGM. 
 The aforesaid documents along with documents referred 
to in the AGM Notice will also be available electronically 
for inspection by the Members, without payment of any 
fees, from the date of circulation of this Notice up to the 
date of AGM, i.e. Monday, 17th August, 2026. Members 
seeking inspection of the aforementioned documents 
can send an email to agmutcl26@adityabirla.com  with 
the subject line “UltraTech Cement Limited 26th AGM” .
8. Corporate Members intending to authorise their 
representatives to attend the meeting pursuant to 
Section 113 of the Act, are requested to email certified 
copy of the Board / governing body resolution / 
authorisation, etc. authorising their representatives to 
attend and vote on their behalf. The documents should 
be emailed to ultratechevoting@kfintech.com  and a copy 
marked to evoting@kfintech.com  with the subject line 
“UltraTech Cement Limited 26th AGM” .
9. Members of the Company had approved the appointment 
of Deloitte Haskins and Sells LLP, (Registration No.: 
117366W/W-100018) as the Statutory Auditors of the 
Company. In accordance with the provisions of the Act, 
the appointment of said Statutory Auditor is not required 
to be ratified at every AGM.

 Further, Members can also use the OTP based login (email

15. Members can access the AGM through laptops, 
smartphones, tablets or iPad. For better experience, 
members are requested to use internet with a good speed 
to avoid any disturbance and frequent disconnections.  It is therefore recommended to use stable Wi-Fi or LAN 
connections to mitigate any glitches. 
 Members will be required to grant access to the 
microphone and webcam to enable two-way video 
conferencing.
16. Facility of joining the AGM through VC/OAVM shall open 
30 minutes before the time scheduled for the AGM and 
shall be kept open throughout the AGM.  Members will 
be able to participate in the AGM through VC/OAVM on 
a first-come-first-serve basis. 
 Large Members (i.e. Members holding 2% or more 
shareholding), Promoters, Institutional investors, 
Directors, Key Managerial Personnel, the Chairpersons 
of the Audit Committee, Nomination Remuneration 
and Compensation Committee and Stakeholders 
Relationship Committee, Auditors, etc. will not be subject 
to the aforesaid restriction of first-come first-serve basis. 
17. Institutional Members are encouraged to participate in 
the AGM through VC/OAVM and vote thereat.
18. Members, holding shares as on the cut-off date i.e. 
Monday, 10th August, 2026, and who would like to

https://emeetings.kfintech.com  by clicking on “Speaker

2026 (9.00 a.m. IST) upto Wednesday, 12th August, 2026 
(3.00 p.m. IST). Those Members who have registered 
themselves as a speaker will only be allowed to speak/
express their views/ask questions during the AGM. The 
Company reserves the right to restrict the number of

 Alternatively, Members holding shares as on the cut-off

21. The facility of e-voting during the AGM will be available 
to those Members who have not cast their vote by 
remote e-voting. Members who cast their vote by remote

remote e-voting shall prevail and vote at the AGM shall 
be treated as invalid.

23. In compliance with the provisions of Section 108 of 
the Act, Rule 20 of the Companies (Management and 
Administration) Rules, 2014, as amended from time to 
time, Regulation 44 of the Listing Regulations read with 
applicable Circulars, the Company is pleased to provide 
to Members facility to exercise their right to vote on 
resolutions proposed to be considered at the AGM by

voting system from a place other than the venue of the

24. The remote e-voting period commences on Thursday, 
13th August, 2026 (9.00 a.m. IST) and ends on 
Sunday, 16th August, 2026 (5.00 p.m. IST). During 
this period, Members of the Company holding shares 
either in physical form or in demat form, as on the  
cut-off date i.e. Monday, 10th August, 2026 may cast their vote by remote e-voting. The remote e-voting module 
shall be disabled/blocked by KFin for voting thereafter. 
Once the vote on a resolution is cast by a Member, the 
Member shall not be allowed to change it subsequently.
25. The voting rights of Members shall be in proportion to

the elimination of several problems involved in the

ONLINE PERSONAL VERIFICATION
50. In today’s ever-changing dynamic digital landscape, 
security, foolproof systems and efficiency in identity 
=== page 16 ===
UltraTech Cement Limited15
verification are paramount. We understand the need to 
protect the interests of shareholders as well as to comply 
with KYC standards. Digital identity verification using 
biometrics and digital ID document checks, help combat 
frauds even when individuals aren’t physically present. 
To counteract common spoofing attempts, we engage 
in capturing liveness detection and facial comparison 
technology.
51. KFin has introduced an Online Personal Verification (“OPV”) 
process, based on liveness detection and document 
verification.
52. Key Benefits:
 - A fully digital process, only requiring internet access 
and a device. - Effectively reduces fraud for remote and unknown 
applicants.
 - Supports KYC requirements.
53. Here’s how it works:
 - Users receive a link via email and SMS.
 - Users record a video, take a selfie, and capture an 
image with their PAN card.
 - Facial comparison ensures the user’s identity 
matches their verified ID (PAN).
54. In terms of the Listing Regulations, it is mandatory to 
furnish a copy of PAN card to the Company or KFin in 
the following cases viz. deletion of name, transmission 
of shares and transposition of shares.

Item no. 3
Re-appointment of Director
The Members at the Annual General Meetings (AGM) of the 
Company held on 12th August, 2020 and 11th August, 2023 
had approved the re-appointment of Mrs. Rajashree Birla 
(DIN: 00022995) as director retiring by rotation and her 
continuation in office as a Non-Executive Director beyond 
the age of seventy five years.
In accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, 
Mrs. Rajashree Birla retires by rotation at the ensuing AGM 
and, being eligible, has offered herself for re-appointment. 
Approval of the Members is accordingly sought for her 
re-appointment as well as continuation in office in terms 
of Regulation 17(1A) of Securities and Exchange Board of 
India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015. 
Mrs. Rajashree Birla is an exemplar in the area of community 
initiatives and rural development. 
Mrs. Birla chairs the Aditya Birla Centre for Community 
Initiatives and Rural Development, the Group’s apex body 
responsible for development projects. She is also Chairperson 
of the Corporate Social Responsibility Committee of the 
Company. She oversees the social and welfare driven work 
across all the Group’s major companies. The footprint of the 
Centre’s work straddles over 9,000 villages, reaching out to 
11 million people. The Group runs 24 hospitals. The Group 
reaches out to well over 100,000 students through its network 
of 54 formal schools and non-formal educational institutes. 
Of these, girls constitute 50%. Both its hospitals as well as 
schools are ‘Not for Profit’ institutions. 
Mrs. Birla is a member of the Advisory Board, Columbia Global 
Center, Mumbai.  She is the Chairperson of Xynteo’s Vikaasa 
Advisory Board.  She chairs FICCI – Aditya Birla CSR Centre 
for Excellence.  Mrs. Birla serves as the Chairperson on the 
Habitat for Humanity India’s IndiaBuilds Advisory Committee, 
and is an active member of the Habitat for Humanity Asia 
Pacific Development Council. Furthermore, she serves as a 
member at the Habitat for Humanity International Global 
Council. Alongside she is also engaged with the Breach Candy 
Hospital Trust.
She is the Chairperson of FICCI’s first ever Expert Committee 
on CSR and is on the Board of BAIF Development Research 
Foundation, Pune, a Trustee of the Gujarat Vidyapith, and a 
Member of the Advisory Committee of the Mahatma Gandhi 
Sabarmati Ashram Memorial Trust. As a patron of arts and culture, she is the President of the 
“Sangit Kala Kendra”, a Centre for performing arts, as well as 
the INT-ABPAA (INT Aditya Birla Performing Arts Academy). 
In recognition of the exemplary work done by Mrs. Rajashree 
Birla, leading national and international organisations have 
showered accolades upon her. Among these the most 
outstanding one has been that of the Government of India 
who bestowed the ‘Padma Bhushan Award’ in 2011 on  
Mrs. Rajashree Birla in the area of ‘Social Work’.  
Most recently she was named the recipient of the ‘Lal Bahadur 
Shastri Award for Excellence 2024’. At the G20 EMPOWER 
Meet in Ahmedabad, the ‘G20 EMPOWER Award for ‘Lifetime 
Achievement’ was conferred upon Mrs. Birla by Smt. Smriti 
Irani, the erstwhile Minister of Women and Child Development 
/ Minority Affairs, Government of India.  Furthermore, Mrs. Birla 
was named as an exemplar in Rotary International’s healthcare 
programmes by the Hon’ble President, Smt. Droupadi Murmu. 
Yet another prestigious award accorded to Mrs. Birla is 
BRICS ‘Living Legend and Icon for Community Excellence 
and Lifetime Achievement Award’, at the hands of the then 
President of India, Mr. Ram Nath Kovind.  
Additionally, for Mrs. Birla’s unrelenting endeavours towards 
polio eradication, she was given the much coveted ‘Polio 
Eradication Champion Award’ by the Government of India. 
Likewise, the ‘Global Golden Peacock Award for CSR’ was 
bestowed upon her by Dr. Ola Ullsten, the Former Prime

Item nos. 5 and 6
Appointment of Mr. Jayant Dua (DIN: 00629213) as Director   
and Managing Director
Mr. K. C. Jhanwar, Managing Director and Key Managerial 
Personnel will be superannuating from the Company at the 
end of his tenure on close of business hours of 31st December, 
2026.
Mr. Jhanwar is a veteran leader of the Aditya Birla Group 
with over four decades of distinguished service within the 
Group. A Chartered Accountant by qualification, he joined 
the Group’s cement business in 1981 as a management 
trainee and has since held a wide range of leadership roles 
across finance, operations, project management, and general 
management in the cement and chemicals businesses. He has 
significant experience in acquisitions and integration. He has 
been exceptional in his networking and relationship building 
skills with customers and other stakeholders and has built a 
strong franchise for the business. He has been a capable team 
builder and has strong people skills. He assumed the role of 
Managing Director of the Company in January 2020. Under 
his leadership, the Company’s installed capacity increased by 
approximately 77%, from 116 MTPA to 205.5 MTPA, driven by a 
combination of capacity expansion and successful acquisition 
and integration. During this period, the Company’s market 
capitalization more than doubled, from US$ 20.85 billion to 
about US$ 42 billion, reflecting sustained value creation and 
strengthened market leadership. 
The Nomination, Remuneration and Compensation Committee 
(“NRCC”) at its meeting held on 6th March, 2026 had noted 
the above. 
The NRCC also noted the structured and comprehensive 
search process undertaken for the selection of the new 
Managing Director, covering identification, evaluation, 
shortlisting, reference checks, among others. The search evaluated a wide pool of senior leadership talent from large-
scale industrial businesses, with emphasis on P&L leadership, 
distribution scale, capital allocation, innovation and ESG 
alignment. The final assessment prioritised candidates with 
proven experience in leading complex, capital intensive 
businesses, particularly within the cement sector, to ensure 
leadership readiness and effectiveness for the Company’s 
forthcoming phase. 
After considering all the above, the NRCC decided to 
recommend to the Board the appointment of Mr. Jayant 
Dua as Managing Director (Designate), w.e.f. 1st April, 2026. 
Further, the NRCC also considered the appointment of  
Mr. Dua as Managing Director and Key Managerial Personnel 
w.e.f. 1st January, 2027 for a term of four years, upon 
completion of Mr. Jhanwar’s term as Managing Director, and 
recommended the same to the Board for its consideration and 
approval. Mr. Jhanwar would oversee a planned and phased 
leadership transition until 31st December, 2026. 
Based on the recommendation of the NRCC, the Board 
appointed Mr. Jayant Dua as Managing Director (Designate) 
with effect from 1st April, 2026. He was also appointed as 
Managing Director and Key Managerial Personnel with effect 
from 1st January, 2027, subject to approval of the Members.
Mr. Jayant Dua is a seasoned leader with 37 years of 
experience. He joined the Aditya Birla Group in 1996 in the 
cement business and spent a decade across functional and 
business leadership roles. Over the last two decades, he has 
held multiple P&L and CEO responsibilities, building and 
scaling businesses across diverse industries such as Insulators, 
Insurance (Birla Sun Life Insurance), Century Cement and the 
Chlor-Alkali Business. In 2023, he was elevated as the Business 
Head – Renewables and Textiles.                 
Mr. Dua brings versatile leadership experience across multiple 
businesses, having led diverse mandates and built a strong 
track record across a wide range of contexts of growth 
and transformation. Mr. Dua is a recipient of the Chairman’s 
Individual Award in the Exceptional Contribution Category 
(2002), the Outstanding Leader (2009) and the Leader of 
Leaders (2022). 
He holds an Engineering Degree from IIT Delhi, MBA from 
International Management Institute and has completed the 
Advanced Management Program from Harvard Business 
School.
Key skills, expertise and competencies of Mr. Dua are as 
follows: Industry Knowledge; Innovation, Technology and 
Digitisation; Marketing; Strategic Expertise; Risk Management; 
Sustainability and General Management.

CHAIRMAN’S MESSAGE
Dear Shareholders,
In a global landscape defined by volatility, geopolitical 
tension, and accelerating technological change, FY 2025 -26 
has been a milestone year for the Group. Our large 
manufacturing businesses have consolidated their leadership 
positions, our newer ventures are scaling with conviction, 
and our legacy consumer businesses are being reshaped for 
a new era of growth. Across this diverse portfolio, one force 
continues to anchor our progress— trust.
Trust is often viewed as an intangible asset. In reality, it is one 
of the most consequential forms of capital an institution can 
possess. In periods of uncertainty, markets can turn volatile 
and competitive advantages can erode. Trust, however, 
compounds. It enables organisations to make long-term 
investments when others hesitate, to navigate disruption 
with credibility, and to emerge stronger from periods 
of change.
For a group such as ours, trust extends far beyond the 
relationship between a company and its customers. It is 
reflected in the confidence of shareholders who support 
long-term value creation, the commitment of employees 
who choose to build their careers with us, the faith of 
partners and suppliers who invest alongside us, and the 
confidence of communities and governments that see us as a 
responsible participant in economic progress. Each of these 
constituencies grants an institution something invaluable: the 
licence to grow.
This is particularly relevant at a time when businesses are 
being asked to do more than deliver financial performance. 
They are expected to navigate technological disruption, 
manage increasingly complex supply chains, create 
meaningful employment, steward natural resources 
responsibly and contribute to social progress. Meeting these 
expectations requires more than scale or strategy. It requires 
credibility built over years and, in many cases, decades.
The strength of our portfolio today reflects the cumulative 
effect of that credibility. It has allowed us to invest through 
cycles, pursue transformation with confidence and attract 
talent, capital, and partnerships that strengthen our 
competitive position. Global Economy in 2025
The global economy maintained its trajectory through 2025 
despite elevated tariffs, policy uncertainty, and geopolitical 
tensions. The impact of tariff measures was less severe 
than projections had suggested, and growth across major 
economies remained broadly stable.
World trade expanded faster than anticipated in 2025, as 
demand for AI-driven capex offset the effects of trade 
policy uncertainty and higher tariffs. The volume of world 
merchandise trade grew by 4.6%, compared to a forecast 
of 2.4%. For the second consecutive year, Asian economies 
were the largest contributors to total world trade volume 
growth, accounting for 3.2 percentage points of the 4.6% 
total — or 71% of the overall increase.
Trade in 2025 was also supported by investment in 
AI infrastructure, demand in emerging markets, fiscal 
and monetary expansion in advanced economies, and 
frontloading of imports in North America ahead of 
anticipated "reciprocal" tariffs from the United States. The 
outbreak of conflict in the Middle East on February 28, 2026, 
along with the partial closure of the Strait of Hormuz and 
damage to energy production facilities, introduced a supply 
shock to the global economy.
India in FY 2025-26: Domestic demand 
carries the economy forward
Against a challenging global backdrop marked by US tariff 
escalations and mounting trade policy uncertainty, the 
Indian economy demonstrated remarkable resilience during 
FY 2025-26. Real GDP growth accelerated to 7.6%, up 
from 7.1% in FY 2024-25, cementing India's position as the 
fastest-growing major economy globally. 
This performance was underpinned by robust domestic 
demand, low inflation, and a broad pro-growth reform 
agenda. On the demand side, private consumption grew 
7.7% year-on-year, supported by income tax reductions and 
rationalisation of GST rates. 
Economic activity was broad-based. On the supply side, 
manufacturing gained momentum, driven by the automobile 
and fast-moving consumer goods sectors. The services 
sector benefited from demand in retail trade, hospitality, 
transportation, and real estate. India also made progress in 
containing inflation, with the headline rate averaging 2% in 
FY 2025-26, down from 4.7% the previous year. CHAIRMAN'S MESSAGE
=== page 30 ===
India's economic prospects for FY27 carry both 
opportunities and risks. Growth is projected at 6.6% by RBI, 
marginally revised down due to the effects of the Middle 
East conflict, which has pushed up global energy prices 
and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. India 
nonetheless remains among the fastest-growing major 
economies globally.
Private consumption is expected to remain the primary 
driver of growth, though elevated global oil prices are likely 
to feed into domestic inflationary pressures. The GST rate 
reductions introduced in September 2025 are expected 
to partially offset this impact. Investment is projected to 
continue, supported by government capital expenditure, 
improved trade access through recently concluded free trade 
agreements, and a stable financial sector. 
India's macroeconomic position, including foreign exchange 
reserves, a narrowing current account, and a path of fiscal 
consolidation, provides some buffer against external shocks. 
The pace of the renewable energy transition, the credibility 
of fiscal policy, and the implementation of newly concluded 
trade agreements will be factors that determine the 
trajectory of growth in the coming years.Aditya Birla Group: In our people we trust
At the Aditya Birla Group, trust is built through experience. 
It is earned in thousands of everyday interactions—when 
people are given opportunities to learn, when careers 
progress on merit, when leaders are accessible, when 
commitments are honoured, and when employees know 
they can depend on the organisation through moments 
that matter.
Over time, these experiences shape how people feel about 
the Group. They influence whether talented individuals 
choose to join us, whether they see a future with us, and 
whether they are willing to invest their energy and ambition 
here over the long term.
The progress we have made across talent, leadership, culture 
and employee experience during the year reflects this 
enduring focus.
Trust in Competence: Helping people  
succeed from day one
The employee experience begins long before an individual 
settles into a role. The quality of hiring, onboarding and early 
support often shapes how quickly people become effective 
and how confidently they navigate a new environment.
During the year, we onboarded more than 11,700 employees, 
including over 80 senior leaders, across businesses and 
functions. Structured hiring and onboarding processes, clear 
communication and timely feedback helped create a stronger 
experience for candidates and new joiners alike.
We also continued to simplify the day-to-day employee 
experience through technology. Mobile-first onboarding 
and AI-enabled platforms such as AVA, which recorded 
more than 700,000 interactions during the year, improved 
accessibility, and delivered greater consistency at scale.
Capability building remains central to long-term success. 
Employees are more likely to perform with confidence 
when they have access to the skills, knowledge and support 
required to succeed. Through Gyanodaya, our Global Centre 
for Leadership Training, and other business-led initiatives, 
we delivered more than 280 programmes, reaching over 
8,500 employees across technical, functional, behavioural 
and leadership domains. Ninety-eight per cent of employees 
accessed digital or blended learning through the Gyanodaya 
Virtual Campus (GVC). In addition, an intense 3-month group-wide learning initiative, the ‘Learning Fest’, engaged 
more than 39,000 employees, a fourfold increase over the 
previous year.
Managers play a critical role in shaping this experience. 
Through coaching, feedback and day-to-day guidance, they 
influence how employees learn, grow and navigate their 
careers. We therefore continue to invest in strengthening 
leadership capability across the Group.
Trust in Growth: Building careers across  
the Group
The strength of an organisation is often reflected in the 
opportunities it creates for its people. During the year, 
more than 6,400 employees moved across roles, functions, 
businesses or geographies. This is, by all accounts, a very 
significant number. These movements reflect the scale and 
diversity of opportunities available across the Group and 
reinforce our promise of A World of Opportunities.
Internal mobility also provides an important measure of 
organisational confidence. Of the 6,400+ movements during 
the year, more than 470 were across businesses. At senior 
leadership levels, cross-business mobility accounted for 15% 
of movements, strengthening leadership depth across the 
portfolio. Nearly 69% of senior management roles were filled 
through internal hiring, reflecting the quality and readiness of 
leadership talent developed within the Group.
These outcomes are supported by a disciplined approach to 
identifying and developing talent. 27% of employees form 
part of the Group Talent Pool. We have also built a strong 
pipeline of future leaders.Our ability to attract high-quality talent continues to reflect 
the strength of our employer brand. Diversity hiring stood at 
19% during the year, while retail businesses achieved 40% 
women hiring. Women’s representation within the leadership 
cadre increased by 8%. Seventy-four per cent of new hires 
were below the age of 35, with Gen Z accounting for 39% of 
all new joiners. 
The Group also received recognition across leading platforms 
including LinkedIn, the Top Employers Institute, Forbes and 
the Financial Times. 
Trust in Care: Supporting people and families
The employee experience extends beyond the workplace. 
Health, wellbeing and support systems influence how people 
feel, perform and engage over the long term.
Through our health, wellbeing and insurance initiatives, we 
supported employees and their families in meaningful ways. 
During the year, more than 8,600 counselling sessions were 
availed by employees, while workmen and staff accessed a 
further 3,100+ sessions, reflecting growing awareness and 
acceptance of mental wellbeing support. In parallel, over 
3,400 eligible employees underwent annual health check-
ups, reinforcing our focus on preventive care.
These efforts are translating into measurable outcomes. 
Among Mumbai-based employees, the proportion of 
individuals in the high-risk category, in terms of health, 
declined from 21% to 10%, while the low-risk category 
increased from 48% to 56%.CHAIRMAN'S MESSAGE

Your Company’s Performance
Your Company delivered stellar growth in FY 2025-26, with 
record net revenue of $10 billion ( ₹88,512 crore) and EBITDA 
of $2.0 billion ( ₹17,598 crore). This represents year-on-year 
growth of 17% and 32%, respectively. Consolidated profit 
after tax (PAT) increased by 36% to $927 million  
(₹8,188 crore).
Growth during the year was driven by timely capacity 
additions and sustained operational efficiency, with 
each milestone reinforcing UltraTech’s commitment to 
strengthening the economic foundations of the nation and 
contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.
In FY 2025-26, your Company commissioned 8 million 
tonnes per annum (MTPA) of capacity across multiple 
locations. The journey continues, with your Company 
beginning FY 2026-27 by adding 8.7 MTPA of capacity in 
April 2026. New grinding units in Visakhapatnam (Andhra 
Pradesh), Shahjahanpur (Uttar Pradesh), and Patratu 
(Jharkhand) have further expanded our footprint. With this, 
UltraTech has achieved a historic milestone, surpassing 200 
MTPA of grey cement capacity a full year ahead of schedule.
Your Company is now the world’s largest cement company 
by sales volume and capacity outside China. At 200 MTPA, 
our installed capacity is nearly double that of the United 
States and exceeds the total cement capacity of the 
European Union. Equally significant, no other Indian company 
has achieved this scale of capacity in any sector.
The 200 MTPA number in my view does not represent only 
our capacity, but also India’s place in the world. It describes 
an India that carries scale with confidence – in its ambitions, 
its execution, and its sense of self. 
With committed investments of ₹ 16,000 crore, we aim to 
increase our total cement capacity to more than 240 MTPA 
by FY2027-28. These investments are guided by a disciplined 
approach to capital allocation and are aligned with long-term 
value creation.CHAIRMAN'S MESSAGE
Our journey is aligned with the scale of India’s infrastructure 
ambitions and its aspiration to become a leading global 
economy. India’s cement demand outlook remains 
structurally strong, backed by sustained investments 
in infrastructure, housing, urbanisation, and the 
energy transition.
The massive expansion of India’s infrastructure over the last 
decade has transformed cement from a basic construction 
material into an enabler of national development. Throughout 
this transformation, your Company has remained a trusted 
partner in India’s development journey. This is reflected 
in our presence in nearly every home, highway, metro rail, 
airport, and port across the country. UltraTech is used in the 
construction of one in every three homes in India. It is used 
in nearly 40% of the concrete roads built by the National 
Highways Authority of India and supports four out of every 
five kilometres of metro rail. Your Company contributes to 
landmark infrastructure projects such as the Navi Mumbai 
International Airport, the Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet 
Train, and the Dwarka Expressway, while also serving the 
aspirations of everyday India through an unparalleled network 
of more than 1.5 lakh channel partners reaching more than 
90% of India’s talukas. Our manufacturing units process 
around 35,000 orders every day, delivering to 30,000 
destinations across the country.
UltraTech also continues to expand its presence in the 
building materials segment. We are on track to commission 
our Wires and Cables business in the third quarter of 
FY2026-27. This will take your Company closer to the 
customer and deeper into the construction value chain, 
strengthening our position as a one-stop provider of reliable 
building products and solutions.
Scaling Up Sustainability
Scale is not the only engine of value creation at UltraTech. 
Your Company also measures progress through the lens of 
sustainability. UltraTech is a signatory to the GCCA Climate 
Ambition 2050 initiative and has committed to achieving Net 
Zero by 2050.
In FY 2025-26, UltraTech significantly expanded its green 
energy capacity by commissioning 371 MW of renewable 
power and 63 MW of waste heat recovery systems (WHRS), 
taking its total installed green power capacity to 1,806 MW. 
At a time when the world continues to grapple with energy volatility, this structural competitive advantage is reducing 
your Company’s power costs while mitigating the impact of 
fossil fuel price volatility. Your Company has committed to 
increasing the share of green power to 85% by 2030 and to 
100% by 2050 under the RE100 commitment.
Progress on decarbonisation has also remained steady, with 
net Scope 1 CO₂ emissions intensity at 538 kg CO₂ per tonne 
of cementitious material in FY 2025-26. This keeps us on 
course to achieve our target of 27% reduction by 2032 from 
the 2017 base year.
Your Company’s progress on sustainability continues to 
receive global recognition. UltraTech has been recognised 
as a member of the S&P Global (formerly Dow Jones 
Sustainability Index) Sustainability Yearbook 2026 for the 
construction materials sector. It has surpassed industry 
averages across all three ESG dimensions — Environmental, 
Social, and Governance. By reducing our carbon footprint 
and pioneering sustainable construction solutions, we 
continue to balance growth with our responsibility to 
the environment.
Conclusion
In a world characterised by constant change, trust, 
becomes an even more valuable source of resilience and 
differentiation. In my view, trust is the currency that matters. 
Over the years, one of the most encouraging aspects of 
the Aditya Birla Group's journey has been the way trust in 
the Group has translated across businesses, strengthening 
consumer affinity, deepening stakeholder relationships and 
reinforcing the resilience of our portfolio. 
Trust, after all, provides a strong foundation for growth. It 
gives us the confidence to pursue transformation within our 
existing businesses and the conviction to build new growth 
platforms for the future. More importantly, it allows us to 
do so with the su pport of those who matter most to our 
success—our customers, employees, partners, investors, 
and communities.

The invisible force 
behind visible progressMESSAGE FROM THE MANAGING DIRECTOR
Dear Shareholders,
The defining feature of the global and domestic economies in 
FY 2025-26 was resilience in the face of volatility. The global 
economy grew by 3.3% in 2025, as shifting trade policies and 
elevated geopolitical uncertainties were offset by hyperscale 
investments in artificial intelligence-led technologies, an 
accommodative monetary stance and fiscal support in 
major economies.
Risks to global growth have escalated with the West Asia 
war. The damage to critical energy facilities and closure of 
the Strait of Hormuz have disrupted supply chains, impacted 
global trade and exacerbated inflationary risks. 
India on the fast track
Despite the uncertain global environment, the Indian 
economy drew resilience from higher domestic consumption, 
policy reforms and sustained government investments in 
infrastructure. India maintained its momentum as the fastest-
growing major economy with gross domestic product (GDP) 
expanding by 7.6% in FY 2025-26.
The West Asia war’s supply-side shocks have tilted risks 
towards higher inflation and wider fiscal and trade deficits. 
However, the external turbulence is offset by India’s 
structural growth story. GDP growth is projected at 6.6% 
in FY 2026-27, led by sustained public capital expenditure, 
steady execution of infrastructure projects, policy buffers 
and domestic demand. Building to grow
Infrastructure and housing growth remain pivotal for cement 
sector demand. These sectors drove cement production 
volumes up by ~6.4% in FY 2025-26. India built over 9,300 
kilometres of national highways in FY 2025-26, while the 
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) anchored housing 
demand to drive cement consumption at scale.
India is the second-largest cement producer globally, 
with cement demand expected to cross 620–630 MTPA 
by FY2029-30, driven by sustained infrastructure and 
housing demand. 
Cement sector volumes are expected to grow 6-7% in 
FY 2026-27 on sustained demand from the housing and 
infrastructure sectors. India’s ongoing infrastructure 
transformation has translated into a robust pipeline of 
projects nationwide. 
The government has allocated ₹ 12.2 trillion to the 
infrastructure sector, ₹ 186.25 billion for PMAY-Urban and 
₹549.17 billion for PMAY-Rural in FY 2026-27, which will 
stimulate demand. 
Your Company’s scale, operational efficiencies and balance 
sheet strength ensure that UltraTech is primed to capture 
these growth opportunities. UltraTech has cemented its 
position as a leading partner in India’s growth, one that 
the nation trusts to reinforce infrastructure projects 
from Assam’s Kumar Bhaskar Varma Setu to the Noida 
International Airport. We also take inspiration from the fact 
that a majority of Indians continue to rely on UltraTech 
products to build their dream homes. 
Cresting new heights
The convergence of our strategic imperatives – scale, 
efficiency and sustainability – resulted in a milestone 
FY 2025-26 for your Company, with new benchmarks 
achieved in our footprint, productivity and brand offerings. 
During the year, we expanded cement capacities by 8 MTPA. 
We also completed the integration of India Cements and 
Kesoram Industries’ cement assets representing 26.3 MTPA 
of cumulative installed capacity. These acquired businesses 
are poised to become earnings contributors with 100% 
migration to the UltraTech brand being completed in March 
2026, and cost and efficiency improvement underway.
"Cement is the invisible 
force behind visible 
progress. As a leading 
partner in India’s growth, 
UltraTech will continue 
to play a pivotal role 
in building the nation’s 
infrastructure while 
advancing sustainable 
development."

With steadfast support of the India 
growth story, we are focused on our 
next horizon with a commitment to 
invest ₹16,000 crore to add another  
37 MTPA and reach 242.5 MTPA 
capacity by FY 2027-28. Acquisitions are not just about adding capacity at UltraTech. We 
only pursue them if there is a strategic fit on delivering long-
term value for the business. Our philosophy is One Company, 
One Brand, One Quality. This disciplined approach is reflected 
in UltraTech’s brand strength, with your Company ranked as 
the seventh-most valuable brand in India and the only cement 
brand among the top 10, by market research firm Kantar.
Our achievements in FY 2025-26 resulted in historic 
financial results across every dimension of performance: 
volumes, revenues, profitability and balance sheet strength. 
Your Company posted record consolidated net revenue 
of ₹88,512 crore, 17% higher over the previous year. 
Consolidated EBITDA rose 32% to an unprecedented ₹ 17,598 
crore on the back of 13.6% volume growth, cost discipline, 
and progressive integration of acquired assets. Consolidated 
profit after tax climbed 36% to ₹ 8,188 crore, crossing the 
₹8,000 crore mark for the first time. Consequently, your 
Company’s net debt-to-EBITDA ratio improved to a healthy 
0.94x as of March 31, 2026, from 1.33x in the previous year. 
These results are the outcome of disciplined strategy, 
relentless execution and an unwavering commitment to 
creating enduring value for all our stakeholders. Increasingly, 
the execution of this strategy is being enabled by a strong 
emphasis on digitalisation designed to enhance operating 
efficiencies, optimise supply chain operations and enable 
better decision making throughout your Company. Ethical 
conduct remains at the core of our governance framework, 
guiding responsible decision-making and fostering stakeholder trust. Our approach to governance is not merely 
about compliance—it is about fostering a culture of integrity, 
where accountability is shared and embedded in every 
business process.
Sustained growth momentum
Your Company has sustained the growth momentum in 
the new financial year. In April 2026, UltraTech crossed the 
200 MTPA mark to become the largest cement company in 
the world by capacity and sales volume, outside of China. 
Crossing the 200-MTPA milestone is a manifestation of 
our ambition to build scale that compounds advantages in 
terms of cost efficiency, market reach, raw material security 
and sustainability. 
With steadfast support of the India growth story, we are 
focused on our next horizon with a commitment to invest  
₹16,000 crore to add another 37 MTPA and reach 
242.5 MTPA capacity by FY 2027-28. 
In line with our bigger ambition to become a leader in building 
solutions, we have also accelerated growth across our ready-
mix concrete, building solutions and products businesses. 
Today, with a pan-India footprint spanning 465 RMC plants 
across 167 cities and a network of 5,568 building solutions 
outlets, your Company continues to deepen its reach and 
customer proximity. We are on schedule to launch our Wires 
and Cables business by the third quarter of FY 2026-27, 
having committed ₹ 764 crore of the approved ₹ 1,800-crore 
investment till March 2026. The intent is to offer our end-
customers a convenient and reliable portfolio of building 
materials and expertise.
Committed to responsible growth
Your Company’s growth is firmly anchored in our endeavour 
to be 'A Force For Good'. Scale and sustainability are not 
competing priorities but twin pillars of long-term value 
creation. This is manifested in our continued progress on our 
commitment to achieve Net Zero by 2050. As of FY 2025-26,  
your Company has achieved a 14.87% reduction in net 
Scope 1 carbon emissions from 2017.
In FY 2025-26, we amplified our efforts across our ESG 
focus areas of decarbonisation, energy transition, water 
conservation, circularity, biodiversity management, safe 
operations and community development.Our renewable energy strategy stands out as a strategic 
lever by providing a structural competitive advantage while 
insulating our operations from fossil fuel price volatility. In 
FY 2025-26, UltraTech commissioned 371 MW of renewable 
power and 63 MW of waste heat recovery systems to achieve 
installed green power capacity of over 1,800 MW. 
Your Company became the first in the industrial sector to 
operationalise a behind-the-meter, round-the-clock hybrid 
renewable energy project to provide uninterrupted clean 
energy without reliance on grid power. As of FY 2025 -26, 
35.8% of UltraTech’s power needs are met from green 
sources, and we are confident of increasing our green power 
share to 85% by the end of fiscal 2030, as targeted.
Greening our logistics is the other pathway to decarbonise 
our operations. In FY 2025-26, UltraTech signed a strategic 
agreement with Container Corporation of India for rail-based 
transport of bulk cement. This will help decongest road 
traffic, lower fuel consumption and reduce carbon emissions. 
We are also scaling up the deployment of heavy duty electric 
trucks for transport of clinker in our logistics operations. As 
of FY 2025-26, our green fleet comprises of 664 CNG trucks, 
28 LNG trucks, and 89 electric trucks.
As a responsible steward of resources, UltraTech also 
achieved 5.8x water positivity in FY 2025-26, that is, we 
harvested and recharged over 5 litres of water for every litre 
used. Balancing development with ecological preservation 
for sustainable growth, we enhanced green cover by planting 
over 6.5 lakh saplings across our operational sites. 
Your Company also advances resource efficiency through 
circularity. During the year, UltraTech utilised 49.83 million 
tonnes of recycled and alternative raw materials in cement 
manufacturing. UltraTech achieved a thermal substitution 
rate (TSR) of 6.6% during the year. We cumulatively co-
processed 1.98 million tonnes of industrial waste, municipal 
solid waste and agro-waste as alternative fuels in our kilns.In a forward-looking move, UltraTech also signed an MoU 
with Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited to explore and 
pilot a first-of-its-kind circularity initiative for used lubricating 
oils to reduce its carbon footprint.
Leading with growth
Your Company’s strong performance at scale, progress on 
sustainability and robust financial health, position it for a 
sustained growth trajectory. 
Cement is the invisible force behind visible progress. As a 
leading partner in India’s growth, UltraTech will continue to 
play a pivotal role in building the nation’s infrastructure while 
advancing sustainable development.

Foray into Wires and Cables
Strengthening the construction ecosystem
UltraTech’s growing portfolio already spans cement, concrete, white cement, 
RMC, wall care products, waterproofing, tile adhesives, and building solutions for 
institutional customers. With the addition of wires and cables, the Company is 
enhancing its presence across the construction lifecycle, offering reliable, branded 
solutions from foundation to finish.
Capturing growth in a high-potential segment
India’s wires and cables market has grown at a ~13% CAGR over the past five 
years, driven by expanding electrification, housing demand and infrastructure 
upgrades. UltraTech enters this space with the advantage of a strong brand equity, 
an established distribution backbone and a deep understanding of evolving 
customer needs.
Leveraging group synergies
The facility will benefit from backward linkages with Aditya Birla Group companies. 
This approach is expected to improve cost efficiencies, ensure consistency in 
quality, and accelerate go-to-market readiness.
Designed for relevance and reach
This diversification aligns with UltraTech’s broader vision of creating an ecosystem 
that supports the country’s infrastructure push while simplifying procurement and 
assurance for customers. The goal is not only to grow share in adjacent categories 
but to create a unified, high-quality experience across every touchpoint in the 
construction journey.From cement to 
building solutions
As India’s infrastructure story gathered 
momentum, our Company evolved with 
changing consumer needs. Cement was 
no longer just a product, but a key enabler 
of the built environment. We entered 
Ready Mix Concrete in 1998, launched 
Wall Care Putty in 2001, and introduced 
UltraTech Building Solutions in 2007 to 
support individual home builders. The 
Building Products Division was formalised 
in 2012 to offer new-age construction 
solutions, followed by the launch of ‘Utec 
by UltraTech’ in 2022, a hyperlocal digital 
platform providing end-to-end home 
building solutions across India.
In 2025, our Company announced its 
entry into the wires and cables sector, 
further expanding its building solutions 
portfolio. The move reflected the growing 
demand from millions of households 
building, renovating, and upgrading homes, 
reinforcing our presence across the 
construction value chain.Contemporary
First and largest single brand retail 
chain in building material segment 
across India
UltraTech operates India’s first and largest single-brand 
retail network in building material segment, offering a 
comprehensive one-stop building solutions stores network 
across 5,500+ stores in 23 states. With over 74% of its stores 
located in rural and Tier-3 geographies, the platform extends 
quality construction products to individual home builders 
through strong partnerships with leading brands.
Building products and solutions

UltraTech proposes to leverage its extensive manufacturing

its Building Products Division, is in line with the Company’s 
strategy to strengthen its position as a comprehensive Building 
Solutions provider, backed by an investment of ~ ₹ 1,800 crore.PRODUCT PORTFOLIO

Expansion of the wires and cables market
The Indian wires and cables market, valued at USD 9.32 
billion in 2024, is set for substantial growth and projected 
to reach USD 17.08 billion by 2032 at a CAGR of 7.94%. This 
surge is primarily fuelled by rapid urbanisation, infrastructure 
expansion and rising electrification across residential, 
commercial and industrial segments. Increasing investments 
in power transmission and distribution, renewable energy 
integration, metro rail networks, data centres and smart 
city infrastructure are driving the demand for high-quality 
electrical cables and wiring solutions. As construction 
activity expands, the wires and cables segment is emerging 
as a critical enabler of modern infrastructure, presenting 
significant opportunities for companies to expand into 
adjacent building material categories.
Our response
Our foray into the wires and cables segment has 
strengthened our building solutions portfolio. Leveraging 
the strength of the UltraTech brand and the reach of our 
distribution network, we are building market presence 
and positioning the Company as a comprehensive 
infrastructure and construction solutions provider.
Increasing per capita cement consumption
India’s per capita cement consumption of around ~324 kg 
remains significantly below the global average of about 
~460 kg, indicating substantial headroom for future growth. 
As infrastructure development accelerates, urbanisation 
deepens and housing demand rises, cement usage is expected 
to increase steadily. This structural gap highlights the 
long-term potential for the sector, as expanding construction 
activity across residential, commercial and infrastructure 
segments drive higher consumption levels across the country.
700 MTPA
Installed cement capacity in India
Our response
To support long-term demand growth, we are making 
investments for capacity expansion, improving 
operational efficiency and adopting measures to 
ensure cost optimisation. Besides, we continue to 
leverage innovation and sustainability to enhance our 
product offerings.Housing demand
Housing continues to be a major driver of cement 
consumption in India. Government initiatives such as Pradhan 
Mantri Awas Yojana, coupled with favourable demographics, 
rising incomes and increasing home ownership aspirations, 
are supporting residential construction across urban and 
semi-urban markets. The growing focus on affordable 
housing and urban redevelopment is expected to further 
sustain cement demand in the years ahead.
2.88 lakh
Additional houses sanctioned under  
PMAY-Urban 2.0 as of February, 2026
Our response
At UltraTech, we are focusing on the retail and 
individual home builder segment, strengthening our 
dealer and channel partner networks across markets 
while offering high-quality products tailored for 
residential construction.MEGATRENDS AND OPPORTUNITIES
Capitalising on dynamic shifts
The Indian cement sector continues to witness rapid growth, driven by rapid urbanisation,  
sustained infrastructure investments, affordable housing initiatives and the development of 
industrial corridors. Construction activity has increased manifold on account of these factors and 
in FY 2025-26, industry volumes were projected to reach ~460-465 MMT, reporting approximately 
6–7% year-on-year growth, after touching ~435 MMT cement production in FY 2025.1
Despite short-term demand fluctuations, fundamentals remain robust, supported by per capita 
cement consumption of ~324 kg in India, much below the global average of ~460 kg. At UltraTech, 
we continue to leverage our deep expertise and market understanding to develop proactive 
strategies for responding to evolving industry requirements.
Rapid urbanisation
India’s urban population continues to expand rapidly, with 
over 35% of the population now living in urban areas, a 
figure expected to reach ~37-39% by 2030. This steady 
migration from rural to urban centres is driving the need for 
housing, transport networks, commercial spaces and civic 
infrastructure. As cities expand and new urban clusters 
emerge, the demand for cement and building materials is 
expected to remain structurally strong.
8,000+
Projects worth ~ I1.64 lakh crore under the 
Smart Cities Mission
Our response
We are expanding capacity to meet rising construction 
demand across urban markets, strengthening presence 
in high-growth cities and emerging urban clusters and 
enhancing our distribution networks to ensure wider 
market reach.Infrastructure push
Infrastructure development remains a central pillar of 
India’s growth strategy. Sustained public investment 
in roads, railways, ports, airports, metro networks and 
industrial corridors, alongside flagship programmes such 
as the National Infrastructure Pipeline and PM Gati Shakti, 
is accelerating construction activity across the country. 
These initiatives are creating significant long-term demand 
for cement, positioning the sector as a critical enabler of 
national development.

consistently expanding our product portfolio to cater to 
specialised infrastructure requirements.

OUR FOCUS W
ITH RENEWED CLIMATE AND SUSTAINABILITY STRATEGY THAT WORKS ACROSS FIVE KEY PILLARSDecarbonisation
Decarbonisation pillar is broadly guided by the SBTi 
validated targets and aligned with the GCCA 2050 Cement 
and Concrete Net Zero Roadmap. Our focus on energy 
efficiency, clinker factor reduction, use of alternate fuel, 
carbon capture solutions and green power is helping us to 
accelerate the decarbonisation journey, in spite of growth in 
scale and production capacity. Through these measures the 
Company is on track for a 27% targeted reduction in Scope 
1 CO2 intensity by 2032 from a 2017 baseline. UltraTech 
is currently in the advanced stages of re-validating its 
SBTi targets to align with a 1.5°C trajectory, reinforcing its 
commitment to accelerated decarbonisation and long-term 
net-zero ambitions. 
Energy management
Across energy management – we prioritise operational 
and energy efficiency improvements, by actively reducing 
specific heat and power consumption, kiln optimisation, 
advanced process controls and expanded waste heat 
recovery systems. Energy transitions are driven by scaling 
renewable energy within our operations, again guided by our 
RE100 goals. We are on track for a 85% green power share by 
2030 across our operations, with a combination of renewable 
energy and waste heat recovery solutions. The Company 
has also piloted India’s first industrial “on-site” RE-RTC hybrid 
solution in Sewagram, addressing critical barriers on round 
the clock availability of renewable energy.
Water Stewardship
The Company also methodically focusses on water 
management, with a specific focus on reducing water 
consumption across its operations, recharging ground water 
by channelizing various surface and ground water sources, commitment on zero liquid discharge and recycling water, 
and building specific water harvesting infrastructure to 
support communities and other stakeholders in the water 
sheds it operates in. The Company has consistently been 
water positive, and is setting new benchmarks internally as 
a result of these targeted initiatives.
Circular economy
By nature, cement industry is at the forefront of circular 
economy driven by systematic integration of waste and 
alternative materials utilisation within its operations. The 
Company has been able to process industrial, municipal, 
agricultural and other wastes across its operations via 
co-processing and other means. Strategic partnerships on 
utilisation of red-mud (waste generating from aluminium 
processing), plastics, municipal waste etc. have enabled 
the Company to utilise more than 49 million tonnes of 
waste and alternative material this year. The Company has 
signed a first of its kind used oil circularity partnership, the 
first in the sector, with one of the leading public sector 
oil and gas companies in India, to further enhance closed 
loop operations. 
Nature and biodiversity
Biodiversity management and nature-based solutions are 
an integral focus area, across our plant operations. The 
Company has managed to facilitate and nurture best in class 
Miyawaki plantations, scientific biodiversity management 
and ecological restoration initiatives across its key locations. 
Clear roadmaps and management plans are being defined 
and implemented across our critical locations, to drive these 
initiatives in a structured manner via cross cutting efforts 
across manufacturing, environment, sustainability, mining 
and horticultural teams.Our ESG approach is embedded across the enterprise – not just focused on 
process or operations, but also beyond into the value chain. 
Measurable goals, accountable governance structure, deeper stakeholder and 
ecosystem engagement have enabled us, to leverage the integrated nature of 
ESG into our overall business model.

We have established a structured ESG governance 
framework to manage ESG-related risks and opportunities 
across our operations and value chain.Environmental oversight and competence
The Board Committee actively oversee environmental risks 
and opportunities across operations and the value chain. This 
includes regular reviews of climate transition plans aligned 
with a 1.5°C pathway, as well as monitoring performance on 
emissions, water, biodiversity and circularity targets.
Board competence is strengthened through:
• engagement with internal subject experts and 
external specialists
• regular stakeholder interactions
• presence of directors with relevant 
environmental expertise
Integration of ESG into strategy and 
performance
ESG considerations are embedded into strategic planning, 
capital allocation and operational decision-making. The 
Board reviews sustainability-linked financing frameworks, 
ESG performance indicators, benchmarking outcomes and 
risk assessments, ensuring alignment with long-term value Board level 
A Board level Committee provides overall guidance and 
oversight on ESG matters.
Executive level
The Managing Director (MD) and the management 
team, provides strategic direction and oversight for 
ESG initiatives across the organisation.
Organisational level
The Chief Sustainability Officer (CSO), along with 
functional heads, leads the execution of ESG initiatives. A Board level Committee provides strategic oversight of 
ESG issues, including climate change, water and biodiversity. 
The Committee meets regularly, with ESG topics forming a 
standing agenda, and reviews performance, risks, targets and 
progress against the Company’s sustainability and transition 
plans. The Committee reports to the Board, with key 
matters presented for review and decision-making, ensuring 
oversight and accountability.
At the organisational level, the CSO is responsible for 
execution of ESG strategy, including climate action, transition 
and adaptation plans, water stewardship, biodiversity 
management and social impact initiatives. The CSO reports 
to Chief Manufacturing Officer, ensuring alignment between 
strategy, execution and performance monitoring across 
operations and the value chain.creation. Our transition plans define time-bound targets 
and milestones, with progress reviewed regularly to drive 
continuous improvement.
Policy engagement for Climate Alignment
We actively participate in industry platforms such as GCCA, 
CMA, CII and FICCI, contributing to the development of 
sectoral standards and sustainability frameworks. Through 
these engagements, we support initiatives such as the 
Net Zero Concrete Roadmap, implementation of NITI 
Aayog decarbonisation roadmap, national carbon credit 
trading schemes etc. We structurally also collaborate with 
various nodal agencies on emerging technologies including 
carbon capture and low-carbon solutions, supplementary 
cementitious materials, innovation challenges etc.

Material Issues for External Stakeholders/
Environment 
We engaged with various internal and external stakeholders 
through a rigorous double materiality assessment involving 
a wide-range of external and internal stakeholders, we have 
been able to identify the topics of material, impacting both 
our business and our external stakeholders/environment or

Summarised below are the key material topics with impact on 
external stakeholders/environment: 
Circular economy 
This year, having partnered with various companies and 
Municipal Corporations, we have utilised 0.6 lakh tonnes of 
industrial waste, 4.40 lakh tonnes of Agro-waste and 20.70 
lakh tonnes of MSW as alternative fuels in our kiln operations 
and captive power plants. This operation not only saves the 
amount of GHGs from getting emitted in the atmosphere 
but also impacts other environmental factors. Land use and 
biodiversity of the adjoining areas are some of the impacts 
mitigated by the diverting wastes from landfill. Environmental impact: 
As per EPA Municipal solid waste ( https://www.epa.gov/
report-environment/wastes ) are the third-largest source of 
human-related methane emissions in the U.S. Methane is one 
of several non-CO2 gases that contribute to global climate 
change. Methane gas is released as wastes decompose, and 
emissions are a function of the total amount and makeup of 
the wastes as well as management facility location, design, 
and practices. Gas emissions can be affected by recycling 
and changing product use. For example, increased recycling 
of municipal solid waste reduces the amount of waste sent to 
landfills while also conserving natural resources (e.g., timber, 
water, and minerals) and preventing pollution by reducing the 
need to collect new raw materials. 
We have estimated that the diversion of agro and MSW waste 
from landfill has resulted in the avoidance of approximately 
1.3* million tonnes of CO₂e emissions. 
This year we have achieved 6.6% thermal substitution rate 
through use of Alternative fuels in our Kilns. 
Stakeholder impacted: Communities, Investors, Customers, 
Suppliers and contractors.
* Based on DEFRA GHG Conversion FactorsDOUBLE MATERIALITY

At UltraTech, advancing sustainability across the supply chain 
remains a strategic priority. While the long-term ambition 
is to integrate ESG principles across all tiers, the current 
focus is on Tier 1 suppliers as the starting point. Suppliers 
are actively encouraged to cascade these practices to their 
own upstream partners, creating a multiplier effect that 
progressively strengthens sustainability performance across 
the value chain.
Key focus areas include:
ESG Assessment of Critical Suppliers
Systematic evaluation of identified critical suppliers 
against defined ESG criteria, enabling risk identification, 
performance benchmarking, and targeted capability-
building interventions.
ESG Screening of New Vendors
Integration of ESG parameters into vendor onboarding 
processes to ensure alignment with UltraTech’s sustainability 
expectations from the outset.
Promotion of Local Procurement
Prioritisation of sourcing from local suppliers to support 
regional economic development, reduce logistics-related 
emissions, and enhance supply chain resilience.
While UltraTech has partnered with specialised third-party 
agencies to strengthen ESG assessment and screening 
processes, the Company continues to take a proactive and 
strategic approach towards enhancing procurement from 
local suppliers.This focus on local sourcing delivers multiple social and 
business benefits, including support for regional economic 
development, generation of local employment opportunities, 
strengthening of community relationships, and reduction 
of supply chain-related emissions. It also contributes to 
improved supply chain resilience and operational efficiency.
Increasing and/or maintaining the share of procurement from 
local suppliers remains a key element of UltraTech’s ESG 
strategy, with sustained emphasis on integrating inclusive 
and responsible sourcing practices across operations.

ENVIRONMENT 
Building a resilient, 
low-carbon future
The Company has been collaborating with 
The Department of Science and Technology 
(DST), Ministry of Science and Technology 
- along with IIT Madras and BITS Pilani, Goa 
campus – to develop indigenous Carbon 
Capture and Utilisation-based technology 
for accelerating decarbonisation. The project 
aims to establish a carbon capture plant with 
1 TPD capture capacity, integrated with an 
existing cement plant, and mineralisation and 
curing strategies to utilise the captured CO2.
At UltraTech, our manufacturing philosophy is anchored on a simple 
belief: trust is built through consistent performance, responsible 
growth, and meaningful partnerships. In all our efforts, our focus 
remains on delivering scale with sustainability at its core.
As we have systematically expanded our capacity and production 
over the past few years, we have simultaneously strengthened our 
operational excellence to set new industry benchmarks. Today, 
UltraTech leads the way in driving energy efficiency, scaling 
renewable energy, and embedding digital innovations. These efforts 
progressively reduce our carbon intensity while enhancing our 
reliability and cost competitiveness.
Our approach is clear and deliberate. We focus on maximising the 
efficiency of our current operations, while speeding up our shift to 
cleaner energy, alternative fuels, and waste heat recovery. To discover 
next-generation solutions, we actively collaborate with technology 
experts, local communities, and our industry partners.

and optimised product formulations. These efforts not only lower embodied carbon in our products but also

UltraTech has continuously enhanced the thermal 
efficiency of its clinker manufacturing operations 
through sustained investments in process optimisation, 
advanced kiln control systems, efficient preheater and

optimising combustion efficiency, and improving overall

pathway towards low-carbon cement manufacturing.
Low carbon process heat 
Cement production requires sustained high-temperature 
heat for clinker formation. Traditionally, this thermal 
energy has been generated through the combustion of 
fossil fuels such as coal and petcoke in kilns and calciners. 
We are piloting Coolbrook’s RotoDynamic Heater (RDH) 
technology to transition from fossil fuel–based thermal 
energy to electrified process heat, using renewable 
electricity to achieve the required temperatures and 
eliminate coal-based combustion.ENVIRONMENT

UltraTech collaborates with 
UCLA to advance cement 
industry decarbonisation 
UltraTech entered into a collaboration 
agreement with the Institute for Carbon 
Management (“ICM”) at the University of 
California, Los Angeles (“UCLA”) to pilot 
a groundbreaking new technology: the 
Zero Carbon Lime ("ZeroCAL"). The ICM 
has developed ZeroCAL technology to 
reduce carbon dioxide emissions from 
cement manufacturing. Processes based on 
ZeroCAL technology can eliminate nearly 
98% of CO2 emissions associated with 
limestone calcination in cement production. 
Your Company will be the first globally, to 
implement the ZeroCAL process at scale, 
representing another significant milestone 
towards its commitment to Net Zero goal by 
2050. The front-end engineering and design 
of the demonstration plant at the selected 
unit is progressing as per schedule to enable 
commissioning at the earliest.
Challenge:  Cement production is a major 
source of CO2 emissions, particularly from 
limestone calcination. Overcoming this 
without disrupting existing manufacturing 
processes remains a key industry challenge. 
Solution:  To address this, we partnered with 
UCLA’s Institute for Carbon Management to 
pilot the ZeroCAL technology. This innovative 
process can eliminate up to 98% of emissions 
from limestone decomposition without 
relying on carbon capture as this process 
electrochemically converts limestone into 
calcium hydroxide without releasing CO2. 
Impact: ZeroCAL has the potential to 
eliminate up to 98% of emissions from 
limestone decomposition. Through this 
collaboration, we are taking a bold step 
towards decarbonising cement and leading 
sustainable innovation globally.UltraTech to implement 
Coolbrook’s technology for 
cement decarbonisation
Challenge:  Traditional cement production 
processes are heavily reliant on fossil 
fuels, contributing significantly to carbon 
emissions. As environmental concerns 
escalate, the industry faces urgent pressure 
to decarbonise.
Solution:  Implementing Coolbrook's RDH 
technology positions UltraTech at the 
forefront of sustainable manufacturing. RDH 
utilises renewable energy electrification, 
effectively eliminating the dependency on 
fossil fuels. 
Impact: The integration of RDH technology 
is projected to reduce coal-based thermal 
energy usage in cement production at 
UltraTech. This move is expected to serve 
as a benchmark for the industry, catalysing 
widespread adoption of cleaner technologies.Energy efficiency   
We are strengthening energy efficiency across our

and wasteful electricity consumption and improve overall

Our cement distribution is supported by an integrated, 
multi-modal logistics network spanning over 30,000 delivery 
locations. Peak daily dispatch volumes exceeding 10 million 
bags are managed through coordinated rail, road, and 
coastal shipping, including captive jetties to efficiently serve 
coastal markets.
A pilot deployment of five electric vehicles at the Dhar Cement 
plant for clinker movement to the Dhule grinding unit resulted in 
an estimated reduction of nearly 680 tonnes of CO₂ emissions.We are the first cement company in India to scale the use of 
National Waterway 1 for gypsum transportation, reducing 
dependence on road and rail while improving efficiency and 
lowering emissions in line with our Net Zero 2050 ambition. 
The pilot movement from Haldia Port to Patna, implemented 
with IWAI, supports the Government of India’s Maritime India 
Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.
We are expanding rail-based logistics by maximising direct 
dispatches, strengthening railhead operations, and increasing 
the use of bulk rakes and specialised wagons. Digital 
tools and network optimisation improve turnaround time, 
enhance asset efficiency, and reduce reliance on long-haul 
road transport.

Net Zero 2050 commitment
Our net zero roadmap reflects a long-term commitment to 
deliver carbon-neutral concrete by 2050. We are guided 
by the GCCA’s Concrete Future roadmap and are aligned 
with the target of limiting global warming to 1.5°C set forth 
in the Paris Agreement. We aim to achieve this by lowering 
clinker content, using low-carbon binders, improving process 
efficiency, using alternate fuel, and advanced technologies 
such as carbon capture.
SBTi validated targets
We committed to the Science Based Targets initiative in July 
2020 and submitted our targets for validation in November 
2020. In March 2021, we became the second Indian cement 
company to receive SBTi validation. We commit to reducing 
Scope 1 emissions by 27% and Scope 2 emissions by 69% 
per tonne of cementitious material by FY2032 from FY2017 
baseline, with targets covering biogenic emissions and 
removals from bioenergy feedstocks.We recognise the accelerating risks posed by climate change and have integrated climate 
adaptability into our operational and strategic planning. As a founding member of the GCCA, 
we are committed to the GCCA 2050 Cement and Concrete Industry Roadmap, supporting the 
transition towards carbon-neutral concrete by 2050.
Internal Carbon Pricing (ICP)
We have increased our internal carbon price by 
3x, reflecting a stronger commitment towards 
decarbonisation. Going forward, a shadow price of 
USD 30 per tonne of CO₂e will be applied to evaluate 
investments and capital expenditure, enabling informed 
decision making. This will be applied uniformly across 
Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, covering 100% of our 
operational footprint.
Life cycle assessment and  
product-level profiling
We conduct ISO-compliant LCA studies for key 
cement categories, OPC, PPC, PSC and Composite 
Cement, to map cradle-to-gate environmental loads. 
The resulting datasets support EPD development and 
inform optimisation efforts related to raw materials, 
fuels, and manufacturing efficiencies.
