Climate risk:  
Mitigation and adaptation
UltraTech Cement's approach to climate action is anchored 
in two strategic pillars: mitigation and adaptation. 
The Company has established a robust governance 
framework to effectively manage climate-related risks and 
opportunities across its operations. Comprehensive climate 
risk assessments have been conducted across facilities, 
identifying key physical perils, with extreme heat and floods 
emerging as the most significant.
Climate governance and strategy
The Company has established a robust ESG governance 
framework, with Board-level oversight of climate-related 
and sustainability matters. Strategic direction is provided 
at the executive level by the Managing Director and Chief 
Manufacturing Officer, while the Chief Sustainability 
Officer, in collaboration with functional leaders, oversees 
implementation across the organisation. Environmental 
and sustainability targets are embedded within executive 
performance metrics to drive accountability and alignment 
with corporate objectives.
The Board and executive leadership provide robust oversight 
of sustainability and climate-related matters. Board-level 
committees review strategic priorities, approve sustainability 
frameworks and monitor progress against defined KPIs, 
with meetings held quarterly and on a need basis. At the 
executive level, performance is reviewed on a monthly basis 
to ensure effective implementation. These governance 
bodies also assess emerging business and climate risks, 
oversee risk management frameworks and guide mitigation 
strategies to enhance organisational resilience and long-term 
value creation.
UltraTech Cement's climate strategy and 
performance
UltraTech's climate strategy aligns with the TCFD frameworks 
and is embedded within its long-term business planning.
We are committed to transitioning to a low-carbon 
business and is actively factoring climate-related risks and 
opportunities into the Company's business strategy. This is 
reflected in the strategic long-term plan, which integrates 
GHG emissions reduction with planned business growth. The 
Company's approach is based on a multi-pronged strategy 
encompassing decarbonising the energy mix, focusing on 
low-carbon products, and diversification of the business across the value chain of the building and construction 
sector. We have evaluated risks across different time 
horizons, which can arise on a short-term, medium-term and 
long-term basis.
In recent years, UltraTech Cement has undertaken 
comprehensive assessments of climate-related risks and 
opportunities, which have been systematically integrated 
into its Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework and 
risk register. These assessments enable the identification and 
evaluation of key climate-related physical and transition risks 
across operations and the value chain.
Physical risks
Physical risks arise from both acute (event-driven) and 
chronic (long-term) changes in climatic patterns, which 
may result in damage to assets and disruptions across the 
Company's operations and its upstream and downstream 
value chain. These risks include extreme weather events 
such as floods, heatwaves and cyclones, as well as gradual 
changes in temperature and precipitation patterns affecting 
operational continuity, logistics and resource availability.
The Company assesses the potential impact of physical 
climate risks through scenario analysis to support informed 
risk mitigation planning and strengthen resilience across its 
operations, supply chain and surrounding communities.
For risks that may not be material in the short term but could 
intensify over the medium to long term, scenario analysis has 
been conducted using four Representative Concentration 
Pathways (RCPs): RCP 8.5, RCP 6.0, RCP 4.5 and RCP 2.6. 
These scenarios help evaluate the potential impacts of 
changes in temperature and precipitation patterns across 
the geographies where the Company operates, enabling 
proactive planning and long-term adaptation strategies.
Our assessment includes both acute and chronic 
physical risks:
Acute physical risks: These risks can potentially impact sales 
volumes owing to the disruption of business operations 
through interruptions in the supply chain, a rise in logistics 
costs, power outages, infrastructure damage and manpower 
shortages, among other aspects. These risks broadly include 
floods, cyclones and droughts.
Chronic physical risks: The potential impact of chronic risks 
such as variation in temperature, precipitation and water 
scarcity has been assessed. A few cement plant sites are 
located in areas with extremely high water stress, combined 
with a projected long-term change in precipitation patterns.ENVIRONMENT
Mitigation
UltraTech Cement mitigates physical climate risks through a 
proactive and integrated approach aimed at reducing potential 
operational and financial impacts arising from extreme weather 
events. The Company undertakes site-specific physical climate 
risk assessments and systematically integrates identified risks 
into its Enterprise Risk Management (ERM), business continuity 
planning and disaster management frameworks.
Progress on mitigation efforts is tracked through key 
performance indicators aligned with the Company's 
decarbonisation and resilience strategy, including:
• Reduction in Scope 1 emissions by 19.28% and Scope 
2 greenhouse gas emissions by 1% from the base year 
of 2017
• Share of renewable energy in total power consumption is 
17.77%
• Share of green power in total power consumption is 
35.8%
• Specific thermal energy consumption stands at 731.3 
kcal/kg of clinker
• Specific Electrical Energy stands at 72.36 kWh/ ton 
of cement
These risks can originate in and impact our own operations as 
well as our upstream and downstream value chains, in terms of 
supply chain disruptions.
Given its pan-India presence, the Company benefits from 
significant geographic diversification of its manufacturing 
footprint. This reduces concentration risk, as disruptions 
at any single location can be mitigated through alternate 
facilities serving market demand. Additionally, a well-
established logistics network, supported by strategically 
located warehouses across the country, enhances operational 
flexibility and continuity during climate-related disruptions.
To strengthen resilience, the Company integrates climate 
considerations into supply chain planning. Annual and seasonal 
weather forecasts are factored into sourcing decisions, 
particularly for fuels and critical inputs, to mitigate the risk 
of delays or shortages. The Company maintains strategic 
partnerships with geographically diversified global suppliers 
and adopts flexible contracting mechanisms to manage 
supply chain volatility. Inventory norms are periodically 
reviewed based on the probability and potential impact of 
disruptions arising from environmental, geopolitical and 
regulatory developments.
The Company also maintains comprehensive insurance 
coverage to protect against damage to physical assets and 
loss of materials due to extreme weather events.To assess medium to long-term physical risks, scenario analysis 
has been conducted using Representative Concentration 
Pathways (RCP 8.5, RCP 6.0, RCP 4.5 and RCP 2.6). These 
scenarios evaluate the potential impact of changes in 
temperature and precipitation patterns across operational 
geographies. The insights derived support proactive risk 
mitigation and adaptation planning, enhancing the resilience of 
the Company's operations, supply chain and the communities 
in which it operates.
Adaptation measures
The Company has implemented adaptation initiatives to 
enhance resilience, including strengthening infrastructure, 
improving flood protection systems and safeguarding critical 
assets. Water risk mitigation includes rainwater harvesting, 
water recycling, watershed development and the use of 
alternative water sources. Workforce safety is ensured 
through heat stress management protocols, occupational 
health measures and emergency response systems.
Key measures include preventive maintenance of critical 
assets, diversification of manufacturing locations, 
deployment of emergency preparedness systems and 
adequate insurance coverage. These initiatives collectively 
enhance resilience and minimise disruptions and financial 
losses from climate-related events such as floods, cyclones 
and heatwaves.
The Company has formulated and implemented a series of 
adaptation measures based on the outcomes of its climate 
risk assessments. As part of its forward-looking resilience 
strategy, the Company plans to undertake comprehensive 
physical climate risk assessments across all existing, newly 
acquired and upcoming facilities over the next five years. 
These assessments will evaluate site-specific risks based on 
hazard exposure, asset vulnerability and potential impact, 
enabling the development of tailored adaptation plans for 
each location.
Following an initial risk screening exercise, Gujarat Cement 
Works has undergone a detailed physical climate risk 
assessment. This assessment identified key climate risk 
perils relevant to the site, evaluated their potential impacts 
on operations and assets, and informed the development 
of a site-specific adaptation plan. Based on this analysis, 
targeted risk mitigation and adaptation measures have been 
formulated to enhance the resilience of the facility against 
identified climate hazards.
This structured, phased approach enables the Company 
to systematically strengthen climate resilience across its 
portfolio, while integrating climate considerations into long-
term capital planning and operational decision-making.

Climate-related opportunities
UltraTech leverages multiple opportunities arising from the 
transition to a low-carbon economy:
• Resource efficiency - We are improving resource 
efficiency through energy efficiency measures, alternative 
fuels and raw materials, higher clinker substitution and 
CFD-based modelling. Together these reduce emissions 
intensity, optimise raw material use and lower operating 
costs while strengthening production efficiency.
 −Biomass helped us avoid 6,50,963.00 tCO₂ emissions.
 −AFR delivered cost savings of C 337 crore.
 −RE helped us avoid 23,48,971.39 tCO₂ emissions and 
save  C392 crore.
• Energy sources - Moving to renewable and cleaner 
energy strengthens our energy security and cuts our 
exposure to fossil fuel price swings. A greater share of 
renewable power and efficient technologies advances 
our decarbonisation roadmap while supporting long-term 
cost stability.
• Products and services - Rising demand for sustainable 
construction materials opens room to expand our blended 
and low-carbon cements. Aligning our products with 
green building standards and customer expectations 
sharpens differentiation and market relevance.
• Markets - Climate-aligned regulations, green procurement 
policies and infrastructure programmes open new markets 
and environmentally conscious customers. Our focus 
on low-carbon solutions positions us well to capture 
this growth. 
 −Revenue share in blended cements: 69%
• Resilience - Building climate considerations into our 
strategy, capital allocation and risk management makes 
the business more resilient. Proactive climate action 
strengthens stakeholder confidence, improves access to 
capital and helps us adapt to shifting regulatory, market 
and technological conditions.
Internal Carbon Pricing (ICP)
Internal carbon pricing is an effective tool to internalise 
the cost of carbon, and to factor the risk associated with 
emitting greenhouse gases. UltraTech has implemented an 
internal carbon pricing mechanism with a defined shadow 
price of USD 30 per tCO2e. ICP is applied in all CAPEX 
decisions across the company. CAPEX proposals submitted 
to senior management for approvals are standardised 
and consist of return-on-investment calculation with and without ICP. This approach allows us to assess the 
environmental impact of projects and capital expenditures, 
incentivise consideration of climate-related issues in risk 
assessment & decision making, enabling more sustainable 
and environmentally friendly decision-making. By assigning 
a monetary value to each ton of CO₂ emissions, we quantify 
the environmental cost of our business activities. This internal 
pricing mechanism serves as a valuable tool for transitioning 
towards a low-carbon economy, Influence strategy and 
financial planning by conducting cost-benefit analysis, 
driving energy efficiency, leveraging low-carbon investments 
& opportunities, reducing emissions in our operations, and 
ensuring preparedness for current and future carbon pricing 
regulations to manage climate change risks. This remains an 
important tool to achieve our climate related targets and net 
zero emission goals.
Value chain initiatives
We continue to strengthen value chain engagement to 
cut Scope 3 emissions and build supply chain resilience. A 
strategic MoU with CONCOR advances low-carbon logistics, 
while we shift our transport mix towards lower-emission 
options such as LNG, EVs and waterways, improving logistics 
efficiency and reducing fuel dependency.
Our footprint is designed to lower value chain emissions: 
grinding units sit close to end-use markets and SCM 
sources, and integrated units near limestone reserves. 
Shorter transport distances for raw materials and finished 
products reduce emissions intensity, improve efficiency and 
strengthen climate resilience while supporting long-term 
growth.
Metrics for assessing climate-related  
risk and opportunities
We track climate performance through a comprehensive 
set of metrics, including Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions 
intensity, energy consumption, thermal substitution rate, 
clinker factor and share of blended cement. We also monitor 
transition risk indicators such as carbon pricing exposure 
and regulatory developments, and assess Scope 3 emissions 
across relevant upstream and downstream categories, 
including raw materials, fuel, logistics and distribution.
We remain committed to strengthening our climate resilience 
while contributing to global decarbonisation through 
responsible, sustainable business practices.Description Mitigation

CCTS compliance
The Government of India’s Carbon Credit Trading Scheme 
(CCTS), 2023 establishes a national carbon market 
to drive GHG emission reductions through tradable 
credits. UltraTech Cement, with 49 obligated units, is 
well positioned for compliance, supported by strong 
renewable energy adoption, higher AFR usage, and ongoing 
efficiency improvement initiatives, placing it on a positive 
compliance trajectory.

doubling energy productivity well ahead of 2035. Operational 
improvements, including equipment upgrades and 
process optimisation, have contributed to reduced energy 
consumption and enhanced efficiency.

EP100 Commitment

target year 2035R&D and process optimisation for 
energy efficiency
Cement manufacturing is energy intensive, requiring 
significant thermal and electrical energy. To reduce 
CO₂ emissions, we implemented targeted operational 
interventions supported by Computational Fluid Dynamics 
(CFD) modelling. CFD optimisation improves pyro-
processing efficiency, reduces thermal and electrical energy 
consumption, enhances alternative fuel utilisation, and lowers 
preheater exit gas temperatures, resulting in reduced overall 
energy demand.
Clinker cooling energy optimisation
In clinker cooling operations, high-speed cooler fans 
consume significant electricity due to inlet turbulence and 
frictional losses. We redesigned the fan inlet geometry 
to improve airflow uniformity and reduce friction. This 
optimisation lowered fan power consumption, enhanced 
electrical efficiency, and contributed to reduced operational 
CO₂ emissions.
Key initiatives implemented across our operations include:
• Cooler modifications through CFD analysis to reduce 
heat and power consumption
• Deployment of Air-Cooled Condenser (ACC) mist cooling 
systems to improve turbine efficiency
• Adoption of Carbon Fibre Reinforced Polymer (CFRP) 
fan blades to reduce energy consumption and 
operating costs

UltraTech has inducted India's first PM

UltraTech operates more than 664 CNG

UltraTech operationalises 
India's first-of-its-kind on-
site hybrid RTC renewable 
energy project
Commissioned at our integrated cement 
manufacturing unit in Gujarat, the project 
will deliver 7.5 MW of RTC renewable 
energy through integrated solar, wind and 
battery storage.
UltraTech has operationalised a 7.5 MW 
round-the-clock (RTC) hybrid renewable 
energy project at our integrated cement 
manufacturing unit, Sewagram Cement 
Works, located in Gujarat. This innovative 
solution integrates solar, using bifacial 
modules with trackers, and wind energy 
alongside battery storage, co-located 
on-site, to provide uninterrupted energy 
during the cement manufacturing process 
without any reliance on grid power. The 
project was executed in collaboration with 
clean energy solutions company Gentari.
Installed as a behind-the-meter system, 
the project marks the country's first 
in industrial power consumption and 
showcases what advanced system 
integration can achieve in terms of 
emissions reduction and energy cost 
optimisation at scale. The project, which 
has been executed with the objective of 
providing uninterrupted clean energy, 
represents a new benchmark in India's 
clean energy transition, demonstrating 
the power of customer-led design and 
integrated system engineering.ENVIRONMENT

Resource stewardship 
Material Issues: E4: Water stewardship
E4    Water stewardship
Water is a critical natural resource across our operations and value chain, essential to core 
processes such as cooling, dust suppression and emission control. Recognising its importance, 
we take a holistic and responsible approach to water stewardship, one that minimises our 
environmental impact, supports communities and strengthens climate resilience.
Our approach to  
water stewardship
Our water management practices are guided by a robust 
Water Policy focused on:
• Minimising freshwater withdrawal through efficient use 
and alternative sourcing
• Enhancing circularity through recycling, reuse and 
rainwater harvesting
• Managing water risks through site-specific interventions
• Ensuring regulatory compliance and safeguarding 
local ecosystems
• Promoting equitable access to water as a fundamental 
human right
In line with global sustainability principles, we recognise that 
access to clean water and sanitation is a basic human right, 
and we continue to support this through our operational and 
community initiatives.

  0.90 Water management
UltraTech Cement adopts a comprehensive approach to 
water management. We systematically identify and assess 
potential water pollutants across operations through Life 
Cycle Inventory (LCI) studies. Key pollutants including 
inorganic compounds, suspended solids and alkalinity are 
evaluated and classified based on source, environmental 
impact and regulatory thresholds, with a focus on minimising 
eutrophication risks.
Water-related impacts are further assessed through Life 
Cycle Assessments (LCA) and Environmental Product 
Declarations (EPD), with findings indicating negligible 
macronutrient discharge. All manufacturing units operate 
under a Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) framework, with 
wastewater treated through Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs), 
Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) and Reverse Osmosis (RO) 
systems, ensuring complete reuse and no discharge into 
natural ecosystems.
1 2 3
Reducing reliance on freshwater
We reduce freshwater withdrawals by 
deploying water-efficient technologies 
and maximising recycling and reuse 
across operations, achieving zero water 
discharge at several sites. Wastewater 
is treated through STPs and ETPs 
and reused, alongside rainwater 
harvesting, reducing freshwater 
dependence. Recycled water is reused 
across processes such as cooling, 
dust suppression and cleaning, 
reinforcing our circular approach to 
water management.Rainwater harvesting and 
groundwater recharge
We implemented targeted rainwater 
harvesting measures including 
conversion of exhausted mine pits 
into reservoirs, installation of rooftop 
collection systems, pond deepening 
and desilting, and construction of 
check dams. These efforts enhance 
groundwater recharge, improve local 
water availability, and strengthen water 
security for communities surrounding 
our operations.Water-efficient irrigation 
practices
In areas surrounding our operations, 
we promote drip and sprinkler irrigation 
techniques, soil moisture-based 
scheduling, and adoption of crop-

communities, we optimise water

with a clear focus on identifying and managing risks, restoring habitats, and protecting biodiversity 
in and around our operational locations. Our approach is governed by the Aditya Birla Group 
Biodiversity Policy and is anchored in site-specific actions informed by rigorous ecological 
assessments, in alignment with our commitment to achieving 'No Net Loss' by 2050. We have been 
partnering with the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), the global authority

management plans and apply science-based methodologies for site prioritisation.

with the mitigation hierarchy. Initial 24 integrated units have 
developed and initiated implementation of BMPs, focused on 
protecting, restoring, and enhancing local ecosystems and 
ecological balance. Sites with high biodiversity value were 
prioritised for detailed management interventions using IUCN-
based methodologies.
To strengthen implementation oversight, we have established 
Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) at eight

expand to all units. Monitoring under these plans includes 
periodic ecological surveys, flora–fauna inventories, 
seasonal habitat assessments, and quarry rehabilitation 
progress checks.

6,57,358 saplings planted

Our biodiversity actions have delivered measurable 
outcomes on the ground. Over 6.57 lakh saplings were 
planted across our units in FY 2025-26, with an 85.48% 
survival rate, enhancing habitat quality and floral diversity 
with a focus on native species. 100% of our quarries operate 
with defined rehabilitation plans, and our progressive quarry 
rehabilitation and habitat restoration initiatives continue to 
expand green cover and strengthen biodiversity protection 
around our sites. Our policies also emphasise restoring 
degraded land, developing green belts, and supporting 
watershed-level ecological improvements.
Biodiversity risk assessment and 
management
Biodiversity assessment methodology
Biodiversity risk and impact assessments were conducted 
across 24 of our integrated units using a science-based 
approach combining field surveys, seasonal monitoring, 
and recognised tools such as the Integrated Biodiversity 
Assessment Tool (IBAT) and the Ecosystem Services Review 
(ESR) framework. These assessments evaluated flora, 
fauna, sensitive habitats, ecosystem dependencies, and 
operational impacts, incorporating inputs from site teams, 
forest authorities, and local communities. We also monitor 
ecological evolution at our sites on an ongoing basis to 
identify biodiversity risks and opportunities, integrating 
findings into site operations.
Expert collaboration for biodiversity assessment 
Our assessments were undertaken in collaboration with 
specialised ecological organisations, including Terracon 
EcoTech Pvt. Ltd., Ecofav Services Pvt. Ltd., and Green Future 
Foundation, ensuring scientific rigour, robust data analysis, 
and the development of site-specific BMPs. Our long-standing 
partnership with the IUCN has enabled joint ecological 
assessments, the application of its Integrated Biodiversity 
Assessment Tool for site prioritisation, development of 
technical biodiversity standards for our operations, and 
community engagement for conservation. We also engage 
with local communities as part of our ecological preservation 
initiatives under our sustainability and CSR programmes.
At UltraTech, sustainability is not a parallel agenda it is integral to how 
we grow, compete, and create long-term value.
Our approach is clear: combine scale with responsibility, and 
performance with purpose. Guided by science-based targets, we 
remain committed to reducing Scope 1 emissions by 27% and Scope 
2 emissions by 69% by 2032. During the year, we continued to make 
steady progress, reducing our carbon intensity by over 19% from 
the baseline.
We are advancing decarbonisation through a balanced portfolio 
of levers. Green energy now accounts for 35.8% of our electricity 
consumption, supported by rapid capacity expansion, while 
alternative fuels, resource efficiency, and blended products continue 
to lower our overall footprint. 
A key shift has been the integration of sustainability into decision-
making. With the introduction of an internal carbon price, every 
capital investment is evaluated through a climate lens ensuring that 
growth today remains aligned with a low-carbon future. 
We are also strengthening circularity and resource stewardship. 
Over 22% of our material inputs are now sourced from recycled 
materials, while we continue to remain water positive, conserving and 
replenishing significantly more water than we consume. 
At the same time, we are investing in the future advancing low-carbon 
materials, exploring breakthrough technologies, and collaborating 
with partners to unlock next-generation solutions for our sector. 
As we scale, our responsibility only grows. Our focus remains on

ensuring that UltraTech continues to lead the transition towards

Integration into enterprise risk management 
and long-term planning
We incorporate biodiversity impacts into our sustainability 
governance framework and enterprise risk management. 
Biodiversity risks, including quarrying impacts, habitat 
loss, and species loss, are identified through site-level 
assessments, and assessment outcomes inform long-term 
land-use planning, quarry life management, and rehabilitation 
strategies. Our progressive and post-closure rehabilitation 
strategies encompass habitat restoration and native species 
regeneration, with all actions aligned with regulatory 
requirements and our commitment to No Net Loss.Commitment to biodiversity conservation
We are committed to implementing best-practice and site-
specific measures to protect biodiversity and manage land 
responsibly, including conversion of mined-out pits into 
water bodies, plantation in voids, ecosystem preservation, 
and maintenance of operational noise levels below 85 dBA. 
We continue to expand green cover around our quarries, 
plants, and neighbouring communities, supported by regular 
awareness initiatives. Through progressive rehabilitation, 
watershed-level ecological improvements, and ongoing 
collaboration with scientific institutions, government bodies, 
and local communities, we remain steadfast in our journey 
towards achieving No Net Loss of biodiversity by 2050.

Environmental restoration and impact 
mitigation
We prioritise environmental restoration through effective 
topsoil management, land rehabilitation, and control of air, 
noise, and dust emissions across mining operations. Mined-
out areas are restored through backfilling or conversion 
into water reservoirs, while green belts support ecosystem 
recovery. Measures such as dust suppression systems, 
enclosed equipment, and noise-controlled operations are 
implemented to minimise environmental impact, ensuring 
compliance and long-term ecological sustainability.Mining activities are governed by a balanced 
approach that aligns operational performance 
with environmental responsibility. Through 
advanced planning tools, efficient extraction 
methods, and digital oversight, we optimise 
limestone utilisation while embedding 
sustainability considerations into day-to-day 
mine management.
Technology-driven mine optimisation
We use digital platforms, precision tools, and integrated 
analytics enable better planning, improved performance, and 
reduced environmental impact across the mining value chain.
Resource optimisation and mine planning
Mineral extraction is guided by detailed resource mapping 
and grade-wise limestone blending to optimise raw 
material utilisation. Advanced planning tools are used to 
align extraction sequences with production requirements, 
ensuring efficient use of reserves while maintaining product 
quality and reducing material losses.
Precision drilling and blasting
Drilling and blasting practices are optimised using AI-enabled 
software and drone-based imagery to improve blast design 
and execution. This approach enhances fragmentation 
efficiency, reduces rework, and delivers cost savings, while 
supporting safer and more controlled mining operations.
Equipment efficiency and emissions 
reduction
Fleet optimisation initiatives focus on deploying appropriately 
sized and fuel-efficient equipment. The introduction of 
95-tonne backhoe excavators in place of larger equipment 
has improved fuel efficiency and reduced operating costs, 
while contributing to lower carbon emissions on a per-
unit basis.Digitalisation of mining operations
Digital platforms are increasingly used to improve visibility 
and control across mining operations. The MineOptima360 
platform integrates the mining value chain and enables real-
time monitoring of equipment performance, production, 
and quality. Pilot implementation has delivered measurable 
productivity improvements and is being scaled across 
additional units.
Data-driven performance monitoring
A centralised Mines Analytics Dashboard has been 
deployed at both unit and corporate levels to track key 
operational and cost indicators. Integrated with enterprise 
systems, the dashboard supports monitoring of equipment 
utilisation, maintenance performance, and productivity, 
enabling informed decision-making and continuous 
performance improvement.
Embedding sustainability across the mine 
lifecycle
Sustainability, safety, and regulatory compliance are 
embedded across all stages of mining operations. Mine 
lifecycle strategies are aligned with national priorities 
and global best practices, ensuring responsible resource 
utilisation, progressive improvement in operational efficiency, 
and long-term environmental stewardship.

Use of supplementary cementitious materials
We are transitioning from clinker-intensive Ordinary Portland 
Cement (OPC) towards lower-clinker formulations by 
increasing the use of supplementary cementitious materials 
(SCMs) such as fly ash and Ground Granulated Blast Furnace 
Slag (GGBS). This shift is enabled through production of 
blended cements including PPC, PSC, LC3 and PLC, reducing 
emissions and improving material efficiency.
Alternative raw and recycled material utilisation
We enhance resource efficiency by integrating alternative 
raw materials into our operations, reducing dependence on 
virgin resources. Mineral-rich industrial residues such as fly 
ash, slag, and gypsum are productively reintegrated into our 
cement manufacturing, supporting circular material flows. 
During the year, 49.83 million tonnes of alternative raw and 
recycled materials were utilised, accounting for 24.18% of 
total material consumption.Co-processing of alternative fuels 
We use cement kilns as high-temperature co-processing 
systems to safely manage industrial, agricultural and 
municipal waste. This enables thermal substitution of 
conventional fuels, while diverting waste from landfill. In 
FY 2025-26, we co-processed 0.6 lakh tonnes of industrial 
waste, 4.40 lakh tonnes of agro-waste, and 20.70 lakh tonnes 
of municipal solid waste as alternative fuels in Kiln and TPP.
Sustainable packaging solutions
We are advancing circularity in packaging by incorporating 
recycled polypropylene (rPP) in cement bags, reducing 
reliance on virgin plastic and associated emissions. This 
supports waste diversion and responsible material use, while 
ensuring compliance with Extended Producer Responsibility 
(EPR) requirements. In FY 2025-26, approximately 1.1 crore 
rPP bags were used, reducing virgin plastic consumption by 
46%, diverting plastic waste from landfills

products. By transforming industrial, municipal and agricultural waste into valuable resources, 
we reduce reliance on virgin materials, extend resource lifecycles and create shared value 
for society. Through co-processing, material substitution, blended cements and innovative

E8    Research and development
Our R&D programmes prioritise development of low-carbon cement and concrete solutions that 
reduce emissions intensity while meeting performance requirements. Innovation efforts focus on 
lowering clinker content, increasing the use of alternative fuels and raw materials, and integrating 
non-conventional materials to conserve natural resources and energy.
Our R&D team
UltraTech has a dedicated R&D function in India, supported 
by a multidisciplinary team focused on evaluating and 
advancing low-carbon technologies. R&D is integral to 
our short-, medium- and long-term strategy, enabling the 
development of sustainable cement and concrete solutions 
with improved energy and resource efficiency, lower CO₂ 
emissions and reduced water intensity. 
R&D programmes are executed in collaboration with 
Aditya Birla Science and Technology Company Private 
Limited (ABSTCPL), enabling applied research and solution 
development aligned with operational requirements. 
Knowledge generated through these collaborations is 
translated into plant-level interventions and customer-facing technical support to accelerate adoption of sustainable 
products and practices. During the year, R&D efforts 
were focused on reducing clinker intensity and enhancing 
the utilisation of supplementary cementitious materials 
(SCMs) such as fly ash, slag, and limestone. Work on grinding 
optimisation including the development of in-house grinding 
aid formulations and refined particle size distribution 
strategies enabled higher clinker substitution while 
maintaining product performance.
In FY 2025-26, we invested ₹ 26.95 crore in R&D, reflecting 
our continued commitment to strengthening our sustainable 
product portfolio.Zero-waste operations
We implement a rigorous waste monitoring and recovery 
pathways over disposal. Fly ash generated across operations 
is fully reused in blended cement production. Overall 
waste intensity remains low at 0.005 tonnes per tonne 
of cementitious material, with 99.99% of waste reused, 
recycled, or co-processed. All facilities are certified as zero 
waste to landfill.
Our circularity performance is supported by systematic 
waste tracking, regular assessments, and third-party audits, 
enabling recovery optimisation, regulatory compliance, 
and continuous improvement through training and 
capacity building.

Process innovation for energy efficiency and 
emissions reduction
Our R&D-driven process interventions focus on reducing 
specific thermal and electrical energy consumption across 
pyro-processing and grinding systems. Equipment and 
system-level optimisations have been implemented for 
pre-heaters, cyclones, coolers, separators, low-NOx burners, 
fans, and drives, enabling improved heat recovery, lower fuel 
demand, and reduced CO₂ emissions intensity.Advanced modelling and digital engineering
Computational fluid dynamics (CFD), process simulators, 
and digital modelling tools are applied across our system 
to analyse heat transfer, gas flow, and material behaviour 
within critical process units in turn supporting optimisation 
of operating parameters, improved alternative fuel utilisation, 
reduction of thermal losses, and enhanced overall process 
stability and efficiency.
Sustainable cement and concrete products
R&D team has developed a portfolio of sustainable products by utilising industrial by-products and construction waste, 
supporting circular economy objectives and low-carbon construction.
Low-carbon concrete
Low-carbon concrete has been engineered through 
optimised binder composition and reduced clinker 
intensity to lower embodied CO₂ emissions. The 
formulation maintains structural performance while 
reducing demand for virgin raw materials and energy, 
supporting lower lifecycle environmental impact in 
construction applications.
C&D waste–based HVFA concrete
This concrete integrates recycled construction and 
demolition waste as aggregates, combined with 
high-volume fly ash to reduce clinker demand. The 
formulation enables diversion of waste from landfills 
while achieving lower embodied carbon and improved 
resource efficiency in concrete production.
Limestone calcined clay cement
LC3 is a low-clinker cement developed using 
calcined clay and limestone to re-place a portion 
of Portland clinker. In-house calcination capability 
supports reduced CO₂ emissions, lower lime-stone 
consumption, and scalable deployment of low-carbon 
cement alternatives.Geopolymer 3D printing concrete
Geopolymer 3D printing con-crete utilises alkali-
activated materials in place of conven-tional cement, 
enabling addi-tive manufacturing with sub-stantially 
lower CO₂ emis-sions. The material supports precision 
construction, re-duced material wastage, and faster 
deployment of low-carbon building solutions.Self-curing concrete
Self-curing concrete is designed to retain internal 
moisture, significantly reducing external water curing 
requirements. This innovation improves hydration 
efficiency, enhances durability, and enables concrete 
application in water-stressed regions while supporting 
reduced freshwater consumption during construction.ENVIRONMENT

E9    Sustainable material innovation
Partnerships to co-develop innovative SCM 
During the year, we signed a consortium agreement to 
co-develop innovative supplementary cementitious materials 
(SCMs) in collaboration with leading start-ups. These 
partners bring specialised technologies to enable low-carbon 
material innovation:
EnviCore:  Converting many waste streams from mining, 
industrial and domestic wastes into SCM using a low-
temperature CO2 mineralisation route hydraulic activity.
Queens Carbon: Low-temperature synthesis of carbon 
neutral engineered SCM from limestone and sand with steam 
and pressure.
NeoCrete:  Nano-activator for natural and industrial 
pozzolans for substituting cement in concrete.
Participation in global innovation 
programmes 
As a member of the Innovandi Global Cement and Concrete 
Research Network, we actively participate in global 
innovation programmes that connect industry with scientific 
institutions to accelerate the development of scalable, low-
carbon cement solutions aligned with our net-zero ambitions.Our value-added concrete  
(VAC) products

across priority logistics routes for

• Closely monitored utilisation of EV fleets

Green logistics and fleet transformation
We significantly expanded the deployment of green vehicles 
across our logistics network. Our green fleet increased to 
781 vehicles (664 CNG, 28 LNG and 89 EVs) as of March 
2026, resulting in significant reduction of carbon emissions. 
It also enhanced cost competitiveness as green vehicles are 
much more economical in comparison to diesel vehicles.Sustainable supply chain framework
Our framework integrates responsible sourcing, risk 
mitigation, and supplier development aligned with ESG 
principles, embedding sustainability across all stages of 
supplier engagement.
ESG-based supplier onboarding
All new suppliers undergo ESG evaluation prior to 
onboarding, ensuring alignment with our sustainability 
standards from the outset.
Supplier training programmes
Through Project Sahyog, we conduct regular training 
programmes to build supplier capacity on ESG practices. 
A vendor support programme, launched in 2023, further 
strengthens awareness and implementation across the 
supply chain.
Supplier assessment and monitoring
We assess over 1,000 Tier 1 suppliers through a structured 
ESG framework, identifying 128 critical suppliers based on 
spend, criticality and supply risk. These suppliers undergo 
multi-tier assessments, including self-assessments, desktop 
reviews and site audits. Suppliers are scored across five 
categories from Elementary to Leader enabling risk-based 
classification and targeted improvement actions.
Supplier engagement and corrective actions
We actively engage suppliers through structured corrective 
action plans, with defined timelines to address identified 
ESG risks. Non-compliant suppliers undergo capacity-
building programmes, including targeted training and 
technical guidance. In FY 2024-25, 23% of Tier 1 suppliers 
were covered under sustainability awareness initiatives. 
Progress is monitored through periodic reassessments, 
ensuring continuous improvement and alignment with our 
sustainability expectations.Supplier capacity building and coverage
In FY 2025-26, we further strengthened supplier engagement 
through structured capacity-building initiatives. A total of 
254 key suppliers were trained under Project Sahyog, while 
100% of critical suppliers were assessed on ESG parameters. 
In addition, 160 suppliers were screened for ESG criteria, 
ensuring alignment with our sustainability framework.
We also expanded awareness initiatives, covering 25.4% of Tier 
1 suppliers, while ensuring 100% adherence to our sustainable 
supply chain framework.
Local sourcing and supplier ecosystem
We continue to strengthen local sourcing to enhance supply 
chain resilience and support regional economic development. 
During the year, 75% of procurement was sourced from 
local suppliers, enabling improved responsiveness, reduced 
logistics footprint and stronger engagement with MSMEs and 
regional vendors.
Sustainable logistics and distribution
During FY 2025-26, we strengthened sustainability across 
our downstream logistics network through operational 
optimisation, modal shifts and digital enablement.
We increased the share of direct plant-to-customer 
deliveries, reducing secondary handling, warehousing and 
associated losses, while improving delivery timelines and 
lowering energy consumption across multiple touchpoints.
Our network was further optimised through digital tools 
to minimise avoidable lead distances and align sourcing 
locations with demand centres, improving fuel efficiency 
and cost effectiveness. Primary lead distance was reduced 
by 17 km compared to FY 2024–25, reflecting improved 
network efficiency.
We continued to optimise our modal mix through greater 
utilisation of rail and coastal routes. It has ensured efficient 
servicing of long-distance markets while reducing 
environmental impact.ENVIRONMENT

Sustainability is embedded into procurement through

Our sustainable supply chain strategy
Supplier assessment framework: We have established an 
ESG evaluation framework aligned with S&P Global CSA, 
SMETA 4-pillar, and GCCA guidelines to assess policies, 
emissions, resource use, safety standards, and CSR practices, 
strengthening accountability and sustainability across our 
supply chain.
Assessing critical suppliers: Critical suppliers are evaluated

our Sustainable Supply Chain Policy and Supplier Code of

by independent audits, site assessments, and ongoing

• Material master consolidation: Standardisation and

Talent acquisition  
Attracting future-ready talent remains central to our growth 
strategy. Our merit-based hiring processes ensure that the 
right candidates are chosen for different roles across the 
organisation. We continue to invest in early-career talent 
as a key feeder channel for leadership pipelines. During the 
year, over 280 early career professionals were inducted 
through flagship programmes such as UltraTechies, ELP, 
Udaan, Ulchemies, CALP. These programmes provide 
cross-functional exposure, technical depth and leadership 
development opportunities, enabling participants to 
contribute meaningfully from early stages of their careers. 
Hiring for UYLP was conducted at premier institutions such 
as DMS IIT Delhi and BITS School of Management.
UltraTech Young Leaders Programme 
(UYLP) 
UltraTech Young Leaders Programme (UYLP) is a fast-
track leadership development pathway designed to 
identify and groom high-potential graduates into future 
P&L leaders. The programme offers cross-functional 
and multi-location exposure, early ownership, and 
strong mentorship from senior leaders, enabling 
participants to build both strategic perspective and 
operational depth. 
Through structured, real-business experiences and 
accelerated responsibility, UYLP cultivates strategic 
thinking, business judgement, and leadership 
capability, preparing individuals to take on high-impact 
roles across the organisation. 
Hiring under UYLP is conducted from premier 
institutes, including top IIMs and IITs, ensuring a strong 
pipeline of high-calibre talent.
Engineering Leadership Programme

Workforce composition
We continue to maintain a diverse and well-balanced 
workforce aligned with our operational and strategic 
requirements. In FY 2025-26, our workforce trends reflected 
a stable operating base with improving quality indicators. 
External hiring stood at 2,803 employees and our overall 
attrition stood at 10%.
Our workforce continues to benefit from a balanced mix 
of experience and emerging talent. The average age within 
the management cadre remained stable at around 40 years, 
preserving institutional knowledge, while early -career 
professionals strengthened the talent pipeline, with 74% 
of new hires in Management cadre below 35 years. Gender 
diversity also improved during the year, with women 
representing 5.3% of the workforce, up from 5.0% in 
FY 2024–25.
These trends have shaped our people strategy across three 
priorities: strengthening retention levers, particularly to 
reduce early-tenure exits; enhancing structured development 
journeys for young talent; and building internal capability 
pipelines for critical roles.

Employee sentiment indicators remained strong, with 98% of

Employee turnover 
Our targeted retention initiatives like providing better 
career pathways, learning opportunities and people-centric 
practices, have contributed to a reduction in overall attrition. 
Our leadership and people teams foster a supportive work 
culture, creating a strong sense of belonging. It is supported 
by our, grievance redressal system that address the concerns 
promptly, enabling employees to build a fulfilling, long-term 
careers with us.Performance management and employee 
value proposition
Our performance management approach is designed 
to reinforce a high-performance culture while ensuring 
fairness and transparency. Through structured goal 
setting, mid-year reviews and annual evaluations, we align 
individual contributions with organisational priorities and 
sustainability objectives.
We continue to strengthen our employee value proposition 
by linking performance with differentiated rewards, career 
growth opportunities and long-term incentives. This 
approach not only enhances accountability but also supports 
retention and sustained performance across all levels of 
the organisation.
Our performance appraisal follows a structured cycle of goal 
setting, mid-year reflection, evaluation and annual review.
1. Goal Setting  – At the beginning of the year, 
employees set SMART goals aligned with business and 
sustainability priorities.
2. Mid-Year Reflection (MYR) – Midway through the year, 
employees and managers review progress and adjust 
priorities if needed.
3. Self-Evaluation  – At the end of the year, employees 
reflect on their performance, impact and behaviours.
4. Manager Evaluation  – Managers assess the employee’s 
performance based on outcomes and how goals 
were achieved.
5. Annual Review Conversation  – Manager and 
employee discuss the evaluation, performance impact, 
development needs and alignment with ABG values.
Performance is reviewed twice a year through mid-year and 
annual reviews, with ongoing feedback enabled through 
‘PingMe’. The pay matrix also considers individual, team and 
business unit performance.
Employees incentives 
We offer performance-linked long-term incentive 
opportunities to eligible employees, including those below 
senior management levels, to align individual performance 
with long-term business objectives. These incentives 
are linked to sustained performance outcomes and are 
designed to promote accountability, retention and long-term 
value creation.Succession planning and leadership 
continuity
We place strong emphasis on building leadership continuity 
through targeted succession planning and capability 
development. During the year, we enhanced visibility and 
depth across leadership pipelines, with 51% of CXO-2 critical 
roles having at least one ready or near-ready successor and 
overall succession coverage for critical roles reaching 54.5%.
Internal mobility remained a key strength, with 64.8% of 
identified successors transitioned into key roles, reflecting 
the effectiveness of our successor identification and 
development processes. These efforts are supported by 
career conversations that help to align individual aspirations 
with organisational requirements. 
Business centre of excellence: It strengthens

and align technical expertise with broader 
business objectives.
Talent councils:  They identify and mentor

Accelerated leadership development:  It applies a 
70:20:10 learning model, combining experiential

‘The Catalyst’, ‘Evolve’ and ‘StepAhead’

Ensuring employee well-being 
Our well-being initiatives are designed to address multiple 
dimensions of employee health and are delivered through 
a combination of central programmes and location-
specific interventions.
Medical care
We support our workforce health through regular 
check-ups, medical support and Tele-consultation 
services and other sickness benefits. Wellness camps 
and targeted interventions are organised to support 
early diagnosis. We also provide employment injury 
benefits due to occupational injuries and diseases.Work-Life balance
We support employees with inclusive leave policies, early 
parenthood assistance, maternity benefits and childcare 
provisions. Our flexible working hours and work-from-
home arrangements in case of emergencies further 
enable employees to balance professional responsibilities 
and personal needs.
Supporting emotional and mental health
‘Life Unlimited’, our Employee Assistance Programme 
(EAP) in India, provides free and confidential 
counselling support for employees and their families. 
Services include 24×7 access to over 100 counsellors 
via phone or email, and urgent cases are addressed 
within four hours, and face-to-face counselling is 
available across 42 locations.
Managing workplace stress
We conduct self-awareness surveys to assess 
employee stress levels. Based on the findings, 
interventions such as yoga sessions and periodic 
wellness programmes are organised to support stress 
management and promote employee well-being. These 
initiatives aim to maintain a healthy and balanced 
work environment.
Comprehensive family benefits
We support employees through family-focused 
benefits including 26 weeks of paid maternity 
leave, with the option of additional leave through 
accumulated or advance leave, and five days of 
paternity leave. We also provide adoption leave, 
childcare leave, privilege leave and transition support. 
Scholarship programmes
Scholarship programmes such as ‘Pratibha’ and ‘AWOO’ 
are provided to support higher education of children 
of long-serving employees, contributing to family 
well-being.
Employee well-being
We follow a holistic approach to employee 
well-being, embedding support across the 
employee lifecycle through frameworks, year-
round programmes and targeted interventions. 
Our approach integrates preventive, curative, 
rehabilitative and promotive care, enabling 
employees to maintain physical vitality, emotional 
resilience and financial well-being.
100%

Employees benefitted from health checkupsFreedom of association and  
collective bargaining
We are committed to upholding employees’ rights to 
freedom of association and collective bargaining in 
accordance with applicable labour laws and the principles of 
the International Labour Organisation. Across our operations 
86% of our Workers are represented by independent 
trade unions. Permanent workmen are also represented at 
national level, and we implement negotiated settlements in 
accordance with applicable laws.
Safeguarding human rights
We are committed to respecting human rights across our 
operations and maintain zero tolerance for forced labour, 
child labour and any form of discrimination or harassment. 
Our company-wide Human Rights Policy is aligned with 
the principles of the United Nations Global Compact and 
the conventions of the International Labour Organisation, 
promoting equal opportunity, dignity and inclusion. To 
support implementation, we have established a Human 
Rights Due Diligence process to identify, assess and mitigate 
potential human rights risks across our operations.
Human rights policy  
Human rights due diligence
We have a comprehensive and holistic approach towards 
Human rights management process to proactively identify 
and assess potential human rights impacts across our 
operations and business relationships. We have developed an 
in-house due diligence tool to identify and prioritise potential 
impacts across our operations and value chain based on 
likelihood and severity. The key steps of our due diligence process include:
Risk identification and assessment
We proactively identify and assess potential human 
rights risks across our own operations, value chain 
and new business relationships such as mergers, 
acquisitions and joint ventures, covering issues such as 
forced labour, child labour, discrimination, freedom of 
association and collective bargaining.
Identification of vulnerable groups
As part of our due diligence risk identification process, we 
identify vulnerable groups that may be disproportionately 
affected by human rights risks, including women, migrant 
workers, contract labour and local communities.
Risk prevention, mitigation and remediation
Based on the assessment outcomes, we implement 
prevention, mitigation and remediation measures 
through defined governance mechanisms, awareness 
programmes and capacity-building initiatives across 
our operations and business activities.
Monitoring and review
We continuously monitor progress on human 
rights issues, with quarterly company-level reviews 
conducted by a central team to track performance and 
strengthen our human rights risk management.
Mitigation and remediation of human rights risks
Based on the findings of our Human Rights Due Diligence 
(HRDD) assessments, we have developed mitigation and 
remediation measures to address potential human rights 
risks. We promote a respectful and safe workplace through 
our Anti-Discrimination and Harassment Policy, POSH 
(Prevention of Sexual Harassment) Committees across sites 
and a dedicated safety function that conducts regular audits 
and corrective actions. Human rights aspects are integrated 
into our supply chain assessments, where suppliers are risk-
categorised and supported through corrective action plans 
to strengthen responsible practices. Responsibilities are 
assigned to relevant teams to implement corrective actions 
and address identified issues.

Our OHS governance structure is anchored by an OHS Board 
and an Apex Committee that provide strategic direction 
and oversight for health and safety across the organisation. 
Together, they review performance, set priorities and ensure 
effective implementation of safety initiatives, enabling 
highest health and safety standards across all operations.
The executive leadership team is directly accountable for 
translating the OHS strategy into actionable plans and 
ensuring its integration with business operations. This 
includes setting annual safety objectives, embedding 
safety KPIs into leadership performance frameworks, and 
driving line ownership of safety across plants, mines, and 
logistics. Regular reviews at Board and senior management 
levels monitor safety performance, incident trends, fatal risk 
controls, and progress on key initiatives, with clear escalation 
and closure mechanisms.
The Apex Committee and senior leadership ensure that 
learnings from incidents, audits, and risk assessments are 
systematically translated into corrective and preventive 
actions through digital CAPA tracking, with periodic 
validation and reporting to the Board. Leadership also drives

Zero Harm objective.OHS policy

to over entire operations, employees and contractors.

Hazard identification and risk assessment
We follow structured incident investigation procedures and 
a comprehensive Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment 
(HIRA) standard. Cross-functional teams identify routine and 
non-routine hazards, assess risks based on exposure, severity 
and probability, and implement appropriate control measures 
to effectively manage workplace risks.
Prioritisation and integration of action plans
Once an incident is reported, the site safety team 
assesses its risk level as per internal guidelines. For high-
risk incidents, the Site Head appoints an investigation 
team to identify root causes. Corrective and preventive 
actions are implemented across operations. Lessons learnt 
are shared through Red Corner Notices (RCN) and Black 
Corner Notices (BCN), with periodic reviews to ensure 
compliance and prevent recurrence.
Procedures to investigate work related Injuries
We follow a structured investigation process for work-
related incidents. A trained team gathers evidence 
through site review, interviews and document analysis, 
applying tools such as Why-Why and RCFA to identify 
root causes. Corrective and preventive actions are 
implemented, findings shared, and progress monitored to 
prevent recurrence and support our “Zero Harm” goal.
Evaluating of Progress against targets
The OH&S Board, chaired by the Managing Director, 
reviews the effectiveness of the safety management 
system every two months. Eight board-level 
subcommittees led by cluster and corporate heads, and 
six unit-level subcommittees led by unit heads, monitor 
safety performance and strengthen key safety elements 
against established targets.
Internal and external audits
We maintain robust internal and external audit 
mechanisms to strengthen safety performance. 
Regular site audits are conducted by internal teams, 
complemented by second-party audits by trained 
employees from other plants and independent third-
party assessments to evaluate compliance with critical 
safety standards.Emergency preparedness plan
Each unit maintains a regulatory-approved on-site 
emergency preparedness plan covering potential 
emergency scenarios and response measures. Roles 
of incident controllers and rescue teams are clearly 
defined and communicated. Employees and contract 
workers are trained for emergencies, and periodic 
mock drills test preparedness of personnel, equipment 
and response systems.
Safety training
We deliver structured safety training to equip employees 
and contract workers with the knowledge and skills to 
identify risks, follow best practices and respond effectively. 
Leveraging digital platforms and simulation-based tools, we 
provide targeted, scenario-specific learning that strengthens 
compliance and safe task execution.
Training detailsEnsuring road safety
We strengthen road safety through a structured programme 
that integrates prevention, real-time monitoring, robust 
infrastructure and continuous training, enabling safer 
journeys for employees, transport partners and the public.
Electronic safety checklist 
We verify driver and vehicle safety compliance through an 
eight-point ‘e-Passport’ digital checklist across all units.
Safety inductions
We conduct safety inductions for new drivers and 
contract workers at cement and RMC plants.
GPS-enabled behaviour monitoring
We track overspeeding, harsh braking, prolonged driving 
and rapid acceleration through GPS-enabled systems.
Journey risk management
We identify high-risk routes and establish geo-fenced 
hazard-prone zones using GPS technology.
Eye2Track app
We monitor road safety KPIs such as speed violations 
at unit level and provide real-time feedback 
through Eye2Track.
Model truck parking yards

Truck yard management

Defensive driving and safety training

Vision
To actively contribute to the social and economic 
development of the communities in which we operate and 
beyond, in sync with the UN SDGs. Our endeavour is to 
lift the burden of poverty weighing down the undeserved 
and foster inclusive growth. In doing so, we build a better, 
sustainable way of life for the weaker, marginalised sections 
of society and enrich lives while being a force for good.
Our approach 
Our CSR approach is anchored in community participation, 
with projects identified through participatory rural appraisal 
and prioritised in consultation with village panchayats and 
key stakeholders. Each year a dedicated annual CSR budget 
is allocated based on emerging needs, with activities and 
spending recommended by the CSR Committee, approved 
by the Board, and monitored through external audits and 
social satisfaction surveys.Our commitment
Compassionate care is at the heart of our CSR policy, 
embraced by our Board, Management, and employees. 
We are committed to creating a society that embraces 
generosity and compassion, and the enrichment 
of stakeholders.
Scope
Our CSR scope covers the complete lifecycle of 
programmes, from planning and design through 
implementation, monitoring, evaluation, documentation, 
and transparent reporting.

7Needs are identified through community consultations and

Projects are prioritised through consensus with village panchayats

using the logical framework approach.
Projects are executed through a strong implementation framework 
and monitoring system, supported by dedicated unit-level teams. 
Social satisfaction surveys and external audits are commissioned to 
assess effectiveness and impact.
All CSR projects and programmes are reviewed by the CSR 
Committee, with execution plans and schedules presented to 
the Board. The Board oversees the annual action plan, resource 
allocation across locations, and impact assessments.
The CSR budget is allocated at a minimum of 2% of the Company’s 
average net profit (PBT) over the preceding three financial years, 
in line with the Companies Act, 2013. The CSR Committee 
recommends activities and budgets, which are approved by 
the Board.
Reporting and disclosure: The annual CSR report and impact 
assessment studies form part of the Board’s Report. Impact 
assessments are mandatory for CSR projects with a budget of  
₹1 crore or more, following at least one year of implementation.
Communication and information dissemination: CSR initiatives 
are communicated through the Company website, Annual 
Reports, in -house journals, and media channels. Details of the CSR 
Committee, CSR Policy, and approved projects are publicly available 
on the website.
Board of Directors
Provides overall oversight and strategic direction for 
CSR. Approves the annual CSR action plan, resource 
allocation, and impact assessments.
CSR Committee of the Board
Reviews and recommends CSR policy, projects, 
and budgets. Monitors progress and evaluate 
programme effectiveness.CSR governance structure 
We follow a structured, community-centric approach for the

Education
We reached over 1,67,322 children this year through our 
network of formal and non-formal educational institutions, 
reinforcing our commitment to universal, quality education 
across our operating communities.
Primary initiatives
School education and infrastructure
Our 37 Aditya Birla Public Schools continued to provide

Keeping girls in school

Healthcare
We remained steadfast in our commitment to building healthier communities, 
ensuring access to preventive, curative, and specialised healthcare services across 
our operating regions. This year, we ensured 100% access to healthcare services 
across all partner villages through an integrated rural healthcare delivery model.
Primary initiatives
Primary and mobile healthcare
Mobile Health Units made 1,711 health visits to remote 
communities, bringing essential medical services to those 
with limited access. We organised 1,094 rural medical and 
awareness camps impacting 1,54,812 villagers, covering a 
wide spectrum of communicable and non-communicable 
diseases including malaria, filariasis, diarrhoea, diabetes, 
hepatitis, arthritis, skin ailments, and gynaecological and 
cardiac conditions.
Specialised medical care
566 specialised medical camps across gynaecology, 
paediatrics, ENT, and dentistry treated 37,150 patients, with 
critical cases referred to Company-supported hospitals. 
Secondary healthcare services were extended to 92,290 
underserved patients through Company-supported hospitals 
and 14 dispensaries and clinics.
Maternal and child health
9,127 women were engaged through programmes on 
antenatal and postnatal care, nutrition, mass immunisation, and escorted institutional deliveries. Over 1,40,328 children 
received polio, BCG, DPT, and Hepatitis B vaccines, resulting in 
near-zero child mortality. 102 school health check-up camps 
benefited 7,752 students, and 43 adolescent health check-
up camps reached 4,316 adolescent girls with preventive 
healthcare services.
Safe water and sanitation
Safe drinking water facilities were installed in 30 schools. 34 
sanitation blocks were constructed to promote hygiene and 
dignity, particularly for 2,556 girl students.
Disease prevention and awareness
115 health awareness camps were organised, screening 2,742 
individuals for STDs, RTIs, and HIV/AIDS. As a Nikshay Mitra, we 
provided nutritional food baskets to all registered tuberculosis 
patients, supporting 1,572 patients into remission.
Physical and mental well-being
24 yoga and wellness sessions were conducted, benefiting 
1,272 participants in physical fitness and mental well-being.

Sustainable livelihoods
We pursued a multi-pronged approach to sustainable livelihoods — strengthening 
agricultural productivity, enabling skill-based employment, empowering women 
economically, and improving livestock management — to drive meaningful income 
enhancement across our communities.
Primary initiatives
Agriculture and natural resource 
development
8,219 farmers were enabled to adopt advanced and 
sustainable agricultural practices through structured training 
programmes and government partnerships. Watershed 
management initiatives implemented in collaboration with 
NABARD benefited 819 farming families through enhanced 
water availability, agricultural demonstration farms, and 
development of community common assets. Sprinkler systems 
and irrigation pumps were distributed to 226 farmers, enabling 
second crop cultivation and increased agricultural output.
Alternative income and value addition
Alternative income generation was supported for 1,460 
families through skill development in mushroom cultivation 
and value addition in turmeric and spice processing, 
strengthening household incomes beyond primary agriculture.Livestock and dairy development
Veterinary health camps immunised 32,881 animals, alongside 
artificial insemination and cattle health services. 1,919 artificial 
inseminations were conducted, resulting in a 22% increase in 
milk production, directly enhancing dairy-based household 
incomes. Model dairy gaushalas were constructed, housing 
3,323 stray cattle reducing crop damage and safeguarding 
agricultural productivity.
Women's empowerment and  
skill development
Vocational skills training was provided to 3,281 individuals. 
Project Saksham trained 350 women in industrial sewing 
machine operations, with 105 women securing industrial 
employment to date. Employability initiatives were further 
extended through coaching for competitive examinations, 
training 30 youths with 4 men and 3 women successfully 
recruited as police constables at the Madhya Pradesh 
Police Service.

Our commitment

Community watershed 
project to revive 
biodiversity and improve 
livelihood 
UltraTech’s Vikram Cement Works in 
Neemuch, Madhya Pradesh, has reported 
encouraging biodiversity and livelihood 
outcomes from its watershed development 
initiative. Launched in 2010, under a public-
private partnership with the Government of 
Madhya Pradesh, through the Government 
of India Watershed Management Scheme. 
Covering five villages, the project developed 
67 water harvesting structures, including 65 
check dams, two farm ponds and contour 
trenching, to address water scarcity, 
groundwater depletion and soil erosion.
A biodiversity study conducted in January 
2025 highlighted improved vegetation 
cover, revival of aquatic flora and the return 
of wildlife and bird species, including 
Nilgai, Golden Jackals and White-throated 
Kingfishers. Improved water availability and 
soil fertility also enabled farmers to diversify 
into Rabi and high-value crops, strengthening 
livelihoods.
Driven by strong community participation and 
ownership since 2019, the initiative supports 
the Company’s Biodiversity Policy, ‘No Net 
Loss’ commitment by 2050 and broader water 
positivity goals.Accolades conferred

Executives in senior management
Fiscal year 2025–26 has been transformative for UltraTech 
Cement. It was a year of purposeful consolidation, disciplined 
growth, and deepened stakeholder trust. As India charts its 
course toward becoming the world’s third-largest economy, 
the cement industry stands as an essential foundation—and 
UltraTech remains privileged to serve as one of its most 
reliable stewards. Every tonne we produce represents 
more than a commodity; it embodies our commitment to 
nation-building, transforming raw ambition into tangible 
infrastructure that powers roads, railways, ports, and the 
aspirations of millions of Indian families.
Scale and discipline hand in hand
We concluded the fiscal year with a global cement capacity 
of 196.8 million tonnes per annum (MTPA), having seamlessly 
woven together the India Cements and Kesoram acquisitions 
with our organic expansion initiatives across multiple 
geographies. Sales volumes expanded by 13.6 per cent to 
154.25 million tonnes, reflecting both market demand and 
operational excellence.
This scaling was neither reckless nor haphazard. It was 
underpinned by financial discipline that our stakeholders have 
come to expect. Every capital rupee was scrutinised; every 
integration executed with surgical precision. This disciplined 
approach preserved our financial fortress: despite an 
intensive capital expenditure cycle, our Net Debt-to-EBITDA 
ratio stood at 0.94x, well within our self-imposed thresholds 
and consistent with our AAA/Stable credit rating—a 
validation of conservative yet dynamic stewardship.
Performance that honours trust
Consolidated revenue from operations grew 16.5 per cent 
to ₹88,512 crore, while consolidated EBITDA expanded 32 
per cent to ₹ 17,598 crore. This exceptional margin expansion 
reflects disciplined cost management, lower energy intensity, 
an enriched product mix, and early synergies from our 
integration of acquired assets.Operating cash flows of ₹ 14,398 crore have enabled us 
to simultaneously fund growth investments and reward 
shareholder loyalty. The Board of Directors of the Company 
have recommended a dividend of ₹ 240 per share, balancing 
prudent capital accumulation with meaningful returns to 
those who entrust their capital with us.
Sustainability: The binding agent of our story
Sustainability, for us, is not a separate chapter in our 
corporate narrative—it is the binding agent that holds 
every chapter together. We are acutely conscious that the 
foundations we lay today must not compromise the world our 
children will inherit. This conviction is not rhetorical; it shapes 
every operational decision, from how we mine and manage 
our natural resources to how we deliver the final bag to a 
home builder in a remote village. Responsible stewardship is 
not antithetical to growth; it is a prerequisite for sustainable 
value creation.
Partnering India’s transformation
UltraTech’s purpose extends beyond financial performance. 
We exist to help build a stronger, more self-reliant, and 
prosperous India—a Viksit Bharat. In partnering with 
governments, industries, and communities on this 
journey, we carry a responsibility that is both humbling 
and exhilarating.
To our shareholders, creditors, suppliers, employees, and all 
who form part of our ecosystem: thank you for being co-
builders in India’s growth story. The trust you place in us is 
the foundation upon which everything we accomplish is built. 
We accept this trust with grace and will continue to honour it 
with unwavering financial discipline, operational excellence, 
and a steadfast commitment to creating enduring value.Mr. Atul Daga

Board accountability
The Board serves as the highest governance authority, with 
Directors responsible for strategic oversight and corporate 
management in line with the Companies Act, 2013.
Board diversity policy
The Board diversity Policy promotes diversity in skills, 
experience, age, gender, cultural and geographical 
background. The Nomination, Remuneration and 
Compensation Committee ("NRCC") evaluates Board 
composition and recommends appointments to ensure an 
optimal mix of expertise, independence and diversity while 
maintaining merit-based selection.
Read here   
Board diversity
The NRCC has formalised a Board Diversity Policy in line 
with Listing Regulations. Our Board comprises diverse and 
qualified members with the requisite skills, expertise and 
competencies, enabling effective oversight and informed 
decision-making.Board tenure and rotation
We follow a structured approach to Board tenure and 
rotation in line with applicable regulations. Non-executive 
and Non-independent directors are subject to retirement by 
rotation and may seek reappointment, with one-third retiring 
at each Annual General Meeting. Executive Directors serve 
fixed terms, while Independent Directors may serve up to 
two consecutive five-year terms, in accordance with the 
Companies Act and Listing Regulations.
Board succession planning
We maintain a structured succession planning mechanism for 
the Board and senior management, overseen by the NRCC 
in alignment with the Board. Internal talent development is 
prioritised to build leadership continuity and support future 
organisational growth.
Management ownership 
Your Company does not have a specific ownership 
requirement, however, your Company has an Employee Stock 
Option Scheme in terms of which stock options / restricted 
/ performance stock units are granted to eligible employees. 
Shares arising upon conversion are held by executive 
directors and senior management.

At UltraTech, the Legal Department serves as an essential partner 
in facilitating responsible business decisions while maintaining 
the highest standards of integrity, transparency, and corporate 
governance. Operating strategically across all organisational levels, 
the team offers practical, business-oriented legal solutions that 
bolster stakeholder confidence and proactively identify or address 
operational and reputational risks.
While litigation is sometimes unavoidable due to the scope and 
complexity of the business, the department prioritises minimising 
exposure by emphasising early risk detection and reinforcing 
compliance measures. The team’s approach is rooted in the principle 
that “prevention is better than cure,” underpinned by the structured 
APP framework—Avoid, Pre-empt, but Prepare to contest. This 
methodology supports the development of resilient and cost-
effective litigation strategies, ensuring timely actions and consistently 
favourable outcomes.
The Legal Department has played a key role in resolving legacy issues, 
executing targeted enforcement actions against counterfeiting, 
and managing complex litigation in areas such as mining, electricity, 
and the environment. Additionally, the team has contributed 
significantly to major transactions, including the successful 
completion and integration of the Kesoram and The India Cements 
Limited acquisitions.
In alignment with UltraTech’s vision of supporting India’s growth, 
the Legal Department also facilitates strategic partnerships, notably 
in sustainability efforts focusing on clean technologies. The team 
provides timely guidance on supply chain challenges, including 
force majeure and economic hardship events, and delivers advisory 
services for emerging markets and international expansion.
Through rigorous due diligence, process standardisation, and ongoing 
enhancement of governance frameworks, the Legal Department 
remains committed to strengthening risk management capabilities 
and enabling sustainable, long-term value creation.Mr. Ashok Kumar P
